| Architecture resources, proposals, semantic decisions, projection compilation, architecture-specific reconciliation | **Architecture Governance / Operations** | Owns outright |

**Authoring test, binding on this section:** if a proposed object would function identically for a non-architecture subject, it belongs to one of the first seven rows and must be **bound, not minted**.

**`G-20` (new) — Architecture Operations is a governed capability under Architecture Governance, not a domain.** It is not a truth-owning domain, an enterprise workflow engine, a generic event platform, a universal queue, or an executive over Platform, Accountability, RBAC or Federation. **Payload-noun ≠ domain** (`D0THES-GRD-026`) applies to my own construction here as much as to labs or Rx.

## §E13.7 — Canonical fact ownership and projection roles

**The law:** *one authoritative owner per fact within a declared scope.* There is **no global canonical state**. Distinctly attributed facts coexist without becoming duplicate truth — which is the same anti-collapse law Identity and Federation already enforce one layer down `[INH]`.

| Fact | Authoritative owner | Class | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source assertion published at origin | Origin namespace | Commitment | Publication ≠ effectiveness anywhere |
| Local admission | **Receiving scope** | Commitment | Sovereignty; typed absence ≠ denial (`§E12.7.2`) |
| **★ R2 — split into four facts, because R1 listed three relations in one "owner" cell and that is the mixed-value-set defect in a denser sentence.** ① semantic commit authority for the revision · ② accountable ownership of the resource · ③ stewardship / custody · ④ canonical carrier where the bytes reside | ① scoped semantic authority · ② accountable resource owner · ③ steward or custodian · ④ the carrier itself — **four questions, four answers**, per the accepted Output-1 eight-relation decomposition | Artifact | Hand-authored, canonical. Naming all three relations as "the owner" rebuilds the concealed sovereign `§E13.16` prohibits |
| Owner decision | The deciding authority | Commitment | Revisable only by supersession |
| Landing | Integration function | Commitment | Proof an **already-accepted** set was applied |
| Effect outcome | Executing boundary | Effect | `outcome_unknown` never projects as `applied` |
| Deployment activation | The deployment | Commitment | Observed, not asserted by origin |
| Impact · conformance · divergence result **meeting a declared determinism contract** | **Nobody — content-addressed** *(the generator contract, publication and custody still have named owners — non-authoritative is not ownerless)* | Deterministic Derivation | Evidence; never authority |
| Effective snapshot | **Nobody — content-addressed** | Deterministic Derivation | Materialized over history + pins |
| Observation | Observer | Observation | Attributed evidence, append-only |
| Detector finding | Detector output, admitted by governance | Obligation | Stable identity (`§E13.4`) |
| Conflict adjudication | **★ R2:** the **rightful conflict resolver under the applicable policy** — `05_supersession_conflict_ledger.md` is the **canonical record home**, and the **decision record** is the exact attributed adjudication. R1 named a *file* as the authoritative owner; **a ledger is a home, never an adjudicator**, and a model that cannot tell them apart cannot say who decided | Commitment | The **decision about** a divergence |
| Impact · conformance · divergence result **when it does NOT meet the determinism contract** | **★ R2:** the **producing actor** — attributed evidence carrying run, attempt, model/tool/runtime version, inputs, uncertainty and reproducibility limits | Observation / attributed analysis | The class model already drew this line and the fact table ignored it. **A conformance or divergence assessment may be a nondeterministic synthesis or an expert judgment; only a declared deterministic result is content-addressed and ownerless** |
| Work obligation | **Obligor** substantively; Build OS for custody | Obligation | Machine findings live in generated artifacts; only **promoted** items enter `08` |
| Correction manifest | Proposing steward | Artifact | A new operation |
| Verification | Derivation + closure Commitment | Both | Result derived; closure committed |
| Receipt | — | Attestation | **References and attests; copies nothing** |

**Generated artifacts own no normative truth — but they are not ownerless.** Every generated class names a **generator-contract owner** (who owns the function and its determinism contract), a **publication owner** (who authorizes a generation becoming effective in a scope), an **operational custodian** (who keeps it running and answers for its liveness), its **source inputs**, and an **accountable verification path**. *The artifact is non-authoritative; the machinery producing and publishing it is not.*

**`G1-FIND-49` — the AB-08 defect class, stated as a rule the estate can check.** No fact of **Deterministic Derivation** class may be hand-authored inside a canonical artifact. Where a derived value must appear in prose, it is a **typed quotation pinned to a source revision**, and the check is arithmetic or referential — **never editorial**. This mints nothing: it is the mechanization of `agent_work_protocol.md:169` (**Single-source law** — a mutable live value is recorded in one owning row and referenced by pointer everywhere else) and of `D0CKPT-GRD-003`, whose **intra-artifact specialization was added 2026-08-08 (`INS-G1B`)** and was boot-visible at Tier 0.5 when the `AB-08` propagation failure occurred on **2026-08-13**. **Two binding rules existed, were in force, were boot-visible, and were insufficient — across three corrective passes that each left residue.** That five-day gap is the entire argument for Output 2, and it is why a documented rule without a mechanical check is `executable_governance_law`'s definition of theater. `[CAN→6 · the check itself · G2 · the validator]`

**Typing is a transitional adapter, declared as such.** Requiring humans to hand-annotate every copied scalar forever relocates the maintenance burden rather than removing it. Target state: canonical constituent identity, generated restatements, automatically emitted source links, compiler-known dependency edges, and linting of untyped residual prose. `[CAN→G2]`

## §E13.8 — Impact and owner-completeness

**Traversal finds edges that exist. Completeness is a claim, not a set.** A graph query cannot find an undeclared dependency, an owner omitted from a descriptor, a liability-triggered authority that is not a graph neighbour, an untyped prose restatement, a subscriber that failed to register, or a deployment whose inventory is stale or forged. Without a completeness claim, an omitted owner **silently disappears from the approval condition** and the system returns a clean closure over a partial graph.

Every impact result carries: graph and ruleset revision · relation types traversed · coverage envelope · unresolved targets · uncovered or untyped surfaces · stale or unreachable inventories · **owner-resolution provenance per authority** · policy-triggered authorities · unowned or ambiguously owned resources · and an explicit posture of `complete_for_declared_coverage · partial · unknown`. **A clean result over partial coverage is never reported as complete.**

The owner resolver composes six inputs: resource ownership · change-class policy · **non-waivable rights and independently liable principals** · jurisdiction/operator/federation policy · exception and risk-acceptance policy · current grant and delegation validity.

**`G1-FIND-50` — the non-waivable authority *requirement* is resolved by policy and never by graph adjacency; the *holder* may still fail to resolve.** **★ CORRECTED IN R1 — R0 fused the requirement with the holder.** Patient consent, professional authority and operator sovereignty: the **requirement class cannot be "not found,"** because its applicability is not a function of whether anyone drew an edge. But the **holder** may legitimately fail to resolve — and **that does not remove the requirement; it blocks `owner_set_complete`.**

**★ CORRECTED IN R2 — R1's list `absent · unknown · unavailable · disputed · lacking_a_current_grant` fused three axes into one value set, and reintroduced `disputed` as a state value that `§E12.7.2` had already repaired.** This arc's most persistent defect, committed again in the finding that exists to separate two fused concepts. **Four independent axes at Output-2 level; no enums settled here:**

| Axis | Question |
|---|---|
| **Requirement applicability** | Is this authority required for this change, under policy? *(Cannot be absent because no edge was drawn)* |
| **Holder resolution / availability** | Is there an identified, reachable holder? |
| **Grant eligibility and validity** | Does the resolved holder currently hold a valid grant? |
| **Challenge / stay / contest** | Is the requirement, holder or decision under an orthogonal challenge? *(An orthogonal resource, never a state value)* |

Any axis can block `owner_set_complete` for a different reason and with a different remedy. Values and resolution algorithms route to **Outputs 3, 4 and `§G1-AUTH`**. The two failure modes are opposite: a missing requirement lets a change through silently, while a missing holder must stop it loudly. Graph absence may downgrade a completeness posture; it may **never** remove a non-waivable requirement from the approval condition. This single asymmetry is what stops an omitted edge from laundering a change past the authority that most needed to see it — and it is the architecture-layer form of `INV-30`'s *every affected owner*, which `G1-FIND-36` already showed CODEOWNERS cannot satisfy. `[CAN→3 · adjacency semantics · 6 · the check]`

**Bootstrap posture, declared rather than discovered later.** Failing closed over a fully described graph is sound; failing closed over the current Markdown estate would block nearly every change. Therefore: closure is required over the **descriptor-covered subgraph** · uncovered or untyped surfaces report `unknown`/`partial` and **never clean** · high-consequence classes remain blocked until covered · lower-consequence classes proceed only under a **named, authority-bearing bootstrap policy with declared residual risk** · coverage expansion is measurable and reported. `[CAN→G2 · coverage instrumentation]`

## §E13.9 — Invalidation, generation, publication

Canonical advancement **logically invalidates** dependent derivations immediately.

**`G1-FIND-51` — invalidation is a predicate, not a stored flag.** A reader determines staleness by comparing the artifact's pinned constituent revisions against current; this requires **no write anywhere**. Storing an `is_stale` boolean would create exactly the independently-writable duplicate state this loop exists to abolish — solving a duplicated-state problem by adding duplicated state, which is `D0CKPT-GRD-003` committed inside the fix for `D0CKPT-GRD-003`.

Then: stale artifacts **fail the current-generation predicate before any replacement exists** · candidate generation is never effective · **partial generation never publishes** · published generation changes through an **atomic pointer swap** · each artifact class declares synchronous, asynchronous or lazy regeneration · repeated generation failure emits a **durable escalated obligation** rather than retrying silently.

## §E13.10 — Operational predicates

Output 4 owns the Change Manifest lifecycle enum. **Output 2 owns the predicates and which object owns each fact** — they are derived over separately owned facts and are never one writable lifecycle scalar. Interface definitions; full algorithms route to Outputs 3–6.

| Predicate | Holds when |
|---|---|
| `impact_current` | The impact result pins the exact manifest revision, base, graph, ruleset and coverage posture currently being evaluated |
| `owner_set_complete` | Every resource owner and every policy-triggered, non-waivable or independently liable authority required for the consequence class has resolved; **no required owner is silently absent** |
| `decision_condition_satisfied` | Current, valid, **independently attributable** decisions satisfy the applicable **versioned decision condition defined at `§4.5`** — its required approvals, refusals, abstentions, required-party participation and **non-overridable rights or duties** — and no blocking refusal, stay, expired condition or invalid grant remains |
| `accepted_historically` | **★ R1 (split).** An authority-bearing acceptance occurred, referencing the exact manifest revision, impact result, conformance result and decision basis. **This is a permanent historical fact and nothing later erases it** |
| `acceptance_currently_usable` | **★ R1 (split).** That acceptance is still usable for a landing or effect **now** — impact, policy, grants, conditions and conformance basis all remain current. An expired grant does **not** erase the decision; it may **block a later effect** and require reauthorization at the point of consequence |
| `landed` | An integration receipt proves the exact accepted set was applied to the named target; **partial or unknown effect is never projected as fully landed** |
| `effective(scope, effective_as_of, recorded_as_of, mode)` | **★ R1:** origin-side validity, local admission and activation, profile applicability, temporal interval and non-revocation all hold **for that scope** — resolved under a **declared temporal mode with both time bounds** (`§E13.5`). One `as_of` parameter cannot answer three different questions honestly |
| `observed` | A trusted, sufficiently current, **admitted** observation covers the named target and generation; **unreachable or unknown is not observed**, and an unadmitted observation is evidence of a report rather than of a target state (`§E13.13`) |
| `conforming` | A current conformance result evaluates the observed target against the effective snapshot under a named policy with adequate coverage |
| `reconciled` | **★ CORRECTED IN R1 — R0 laundered unresolved work into reconciliation.** Declared, landed, effective, generated and observed facts **agree**, **or** every remaining difference is a **current, valid, explicitly authorized** variation / transition-skew / degraded posture **within its permitted envelope**. **★ R2 — a degraded posture satisfies `reconciled` only where the effective declared target *is* the degraded posture, that target's required facts agree, and every unknown or verification debt remains separately visible. Authorization to proceed is never proof of conformance** — R1 fixed the open-obligation laundering and left the same laundering one clause over, through degraded authorization. R0 also admitted *"open obligation"* as a satisfying disjunct, which means **every defect having a ticket would report a fleet as reconciled** — the single most dangerous metric error available at fleet scale, because it makes a degrading estate look healthy to exactly the people who would otherwise intervene |
| `accounted_for` | **★ R1 (new, and it is what R0 actually meant).** Every divergence is known, attributed and owned — with or without an open obligation. **`accounted_for` and `reconciled` are independent:** a well-run estate may be fully accounted-for and not reconciled, and that is an honest and reportable state |
| `remediation_active` | **★ R1 (new).** A discharge attempt is currently live against the open obligation. Distinguishes *owned and being worked* from *owned and parked* |
| `stale` | The result's pinned source generation no longer matches the generation the query requires |

**Each constituent decision remains owned by its deciding authority.** Decision-policy ownership and versioning, thresholds or quorum **where a body type actually has them**, abstention, delegation and substitution, tie and deadlock, appeal and reopening remain **`§G1-AUTH`** or domain-policy semantics. This predicate composes them; it does not invent them, and `§4.5`'s rule that **thresholds are profile configuration** is inherited rather than restated.

**A materialized current-state projection is permitted for latency and forbidden as a second writable truth:** derived, generation-stamped, deterministically re-derivable, invalidatable — never independently editable.

## §E13.11 — Durable work, replacement, semantic collision, degraded mode

**No generic queue is minted, and no generic `work` object is introduced.** **Build OS / Agent Work Protocol owns** work-package and lane identity, custody, transfer, one-active-writer, stale-resumption prohibition, state and closure. Output 2's **durable owed work is an `obligation`**; **`operation_id` correlates the intended architecture change**; **runs and attempts are Agent Runtime objects**. Those are four distinct identities and **no fifth identity sits above them** — ending, moving or replacing one carrier advances none of the others unless that object's own condition is satisfied (`§E13.27.5`).

Architecture work binds to Build OS and Agent Runtime for stable work identity · dependency readiness · priority · claim and lease · heartbeat · attempt · timeout · retry and backoff · cancellation and revocation · dead-letter and escalation · replacement actor · result publication · terminal or compensating disposition. Build OS `10` already names claims, leases, merge queues and collision detection as **a maturity target rather than an accepted tool architecture**; Output 2 states how architecture work *uses* them and does not pretend they exist.

**Semantic collision is the architecture-specific addition.** Base movement and file disjointness are not collision control: two proposals can be file-disjoint and semantically contradictory, based on different owner or policy revisions, modifying different descriptions of the same logical resource, individually conforming and jointly invalid, or competing to supersede the same relation. The envelope needs a protected **logical** resource set · overlapping-operation detection · atomicity groups · ordering dependencies · a semantic conflict object · a rightful resolver · re-evaluation conditions. **Git and merge queues are adapters underneath it, never the model** — and this is where the arc's own `git-is-a-carrier` law becomes operational rather than rhetorical.

**`G1-FIND-52` — the loop must be able to not run, and neither review raised it.** At scale the conformance engine will be down, the graph will be mid-migration, an inventory will be unreachable. *"Everything blocks"* puts a single point of failure in the constitution; *"proceed unverified"* puts a bypass in it. The third answer is the **minimum-equipment-list posture the estate's own airplane comparator already supplies** (thesis §3.5 Lens B — fail-safe, checklists, black-box): a change may proceed under a **named degraded-mode authority** carrying a recorded **verification debt** that is itself a tracked obligation. Bounded by: named authority · consequence-class ceiling · explicit scope · expiry · compensating controls · discharge deadline · escalation. **Verification debt may never waive a non-derogable authority, a patient-safety floor, a professional duty, a consent requirement or an independently borne duty.** EXISTS-AS `verification_debt_as_capacity_control` (wave 6, `EVRUN-2026-000011` #296) — sharpened, not minted.

**★ CORRECTED IN R1 — R0's *"fail-closed if undischarged"* is incoherent once an effect is irreversible.** A single expiry action assumes the world can always be restored. After a forward-only migration, an externally committed effect or a delivered emission, closing the gate changes nothing that already happened. **Expiry therefore selects from what remains actually available:** block further promotion · quarantine the affected scope · **withdraw the conformance attestation** · safe halt · compensating action · forward correction · escalation to the accountable principal.

**★ CORRECTED IN R2 — R1 said *"the first four are always available,"* which is false and dangerous in exactly the domain OMNI serves.** Availability is conditioned on **authority, custody, reversibility and safety**: safe halt may itself cause harm in care; quarantine may be technically or legally unavailable; OMNI may not control the external system at all. **The minimum invariant, which genuinely always holds:** OMNI **stops further effects it still controls**, **withdraws claims it no longer has evidence to make**, **preserves the debt**, and **escalates**. Containment, halt, compensation, rollback and forward correction are conditional. An expiry path that cannot name which action applies *and why it is available* is a promise rather than a control. `[CAN→5 · migration · Platform · compensation]` `[CAN→6 · discharge proof · G2]`

## §E13.12 — Decision-condition interfaces

**These interfaces specialize `§4.5`'s decision-condition inputs through `§4.6`'s seat, accountable-principal, exercising-actor and grant bindings. They are not a second authority model.**

Interfaces required here; **substantive semantics bound to `§G1-AUTH`, not invented**: approval · refusal · abstention · absent or unavailable authority · delegate or substitute · conditional approval and condition expiry · decision expiry · revoked grant · conflicting decision revisions · challenge and stay · emergency action · **point-of-consequence reauthorization** · partial acceptance and splitting.

**`G1-FIND-53` — two kinds of blocking refusal, and a model with one type will silently treat them alike.**

| | **Delegated / revocable gate authority** | **Non-waivable or non-derogable independently held right, duty or authority** |
|---|---|---|
| Example | A review function whose refusal blocks | Patient consent refusal · professional clinical duty · operator sovereignty over local admission |
| Held by | A delegate, at the delegator's discretion | The principal, by law, contract, role or duty |
| Can be ended | **Yes — prospectively**, by withdrawing or replacing the delegation | **Yes — but only by the rightful holder or the governing external basis, prospectively, with history preserved.** A patient withdrawing consent is the paradigm case; licences expire; duties end when the governed condition or governing law ends; an operator may make a new admission decision. **Permanence is not the invariant — non-derogability by others is** |
| Recorded refusal | **Survives.** Ending a delegation never rewrites a recorded refusal as though it never occurred | Survives. **★ R2 — narrowed: cessation *alone* does not erase history and does not *automatically* invalidate prior acts.** R1 said such acts are *"not retroactively invalidated,"* which announces a universal legal rule Output 2 has no standing to make. A separate governing law, an adjudication, a determination that the original authority was invalid, or an explicitly retroactive authority-bearing decision **may** change their treatment (`§E13.5` supplies the temporal machinery; the substantive rule is not ours) |
| Fungibility | Not routable around while the delegation stands | **★ R1 — the durable invariant is not permanence, it is non-derogability by others: no other participant may waive, outvote, route around or silently time it out while it remains effective.** |

Both produce a blocking refusal; the failure mode of confusing them runs in exactly one direction. **The vocabulary discipline matters too — do not call every professional duty or operator sovereignty claim a "right."** They are independently borne duties and authorities, and flattening them into "rights" is the value-collapse defect this arc has now repaired six times. Where a waiver exists at all, **the waiver holder is named**. `[CAN→§G1-AUTH · 3 · 6]`

## §E13.13 — Observation and evidence trust

An observation carries: observer and workload identity · target and scope · acquisition method · **observed time and recorded time** · freshness · coverage and unreachable areas · tool, runtime and configuration revision · input and artifact digests · instrumentation health · uncertainty · corroboration or contradiction · retention and revocation · notification and subscription · priority · dedup and coalescing · escalation.

**Machine evidence is evidence.** A signature proves custody, not correctness; a tool version proves provenance, not accuracy.

**`G1-FIND-59` (new in R1) — an observation event and a claim about the target are two different facts, and R0's class definition undercut its own field list.** R0 said observation failure means *"coverage gap or unreachable target — not a wrong answer,"* which cannot survive the forged, incorrect, stale or mis-scoped evidence the charge explicitly requires. **`Observer O reported X at T` is establishable. `Target S was in state X` is not, by the same event.** Two objects:

| Object | Establishes | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| **Observation event** | That an acquisition or assertion occurred | Source-issued event identity · acquirer · target · method · observed and recorded time · provenance · delivery attempt |
| **Evidence admission** | That the event is usable as evidence *of target state* for **this** decision | Identity and signature validity · correct target binding · instrumentation health · source currency · coverage sufficiency · integrity · corroboration or contradiction · admissibility for the named conformance decision |

**The event is preserved even when admission fails** — a rejected or forged observation is itself evidence about the observer, and deleting it destroys the only trace of the attempt.

**Evidence admission is three facts, not one polymorphic object.** An earlier formulation defined a single identity as *"Commitment **or** Deterministic Derivation,"* which violates the one-signature-per-act rule: consequence does not convert an evaluation into a decision.

| Fact | Signature | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| **Admissibility evaluation result** | Deterministic derivation | Pinned observation-event revision · policy/ruleset version · purpose · temporal bounds · content-addressed result |
| **Admission decision** | Commitment | Admitting authority · basis · revision and supersession history — **only where judgment is required** |
| **Effective admission** | Derived predicate | Resolves from **either** a current attributed decision **or** an accepted policy plus a current deterministic result |

**An accepted policy may pre-authorize automatic recognition — the policy's prior acceptance supplies the authority, and the per-instance evaluation stays a derivation.** It does not become a commitment because something downstream depends on it. **Admission is per-decision, not global:** the same observation may be admissible for a low-consequence check and inadmissible for a landing gate. Output 6 owns the algorithm; Output 2 owns the identities and their rightful owners. `[CAN→6 · admission criteria]`

**Observation identity is origin-qualified under anti-equivocation.** A source-issued identity alone is not globally unambiguous and does not stop a defective or hostile source reusing one identifier for different content. Identity is `observer/source namespace + source event identity`, under the **anti-equivocation rule this carrier already established at `§E12.7.3`** — one identifier may never resolve to two contents, and matching content implies neither shared identity nor shared authority. Ingestion and delivery-attempt identity are retained separately. `[INH]` from the existing rule; nothing new minted.

**`G1-FIND-54` — observer independence is a property of the observation *set*, and R0's own formulation destroyed evidence to make that point.** **★ CORRECTED IN R1.** R0 said twenty correlated observers are *"one observation with twenty timestamps."* That is worse than the error it was fixing: collapsing the events discards detector consistency, disagreement between supposedly identical detectors, timing, observer behaviour and liveness — **real data deleted to protect an inference**, which is `§7.1` item 6's *narrative revision destroys evidence* committed in the section about evidence trust. Corrected: **twenty separately attributable observation events in one declared dependence/correlation cluster, carrying no claim of twenty-fold independent corroboration.** The invariant was always about **corroboration weight**, never about event identity. This is `§E12.2`'s independence-per-claim rule applied to machine evidence, and the same law wave 6 states as *parallel agents ≠ evidentiary independence*. `[CAN→6]`

**`G1-FIND-60` (new in R1) — the no-auto-apply rule was bypassable by auto-creating obligations.** R0 had the observer never *applying* a change, while its controller emitted **substantive obligations** directly — so a detector could not edit architecture but could unilaterally place a binding duty on an owner, which is authority by another route. **Corrected: a controller emits observations, evidence and *candidate* findings only.** A candidate becomes a substantive obligation solely through an **authority-bearing admission**, or through an **already-accepted deterministic policy** that pre-authorizes automatic admission for that defect class. This preserves the raw anchor's own position (`EVSRC-2026-000188_TK.md`: emits work items; auto-promotion prohibited) rather than honouring it in one clause and defeating it in the next. `[CAN→6 · admission policy · Accountability threshold]`

## §E13.14 — Review admission and independence requirements

**Admission before review.** A proposal that has not arrived carrying declared class and consequence · pinned base · valid schema · impact result and coverage posture · required-owner set with provenance · **conformance preflight result** · collision check · rollout scope · rollback/compensation/forward-only posture · cited evidence · stated uncertainty — **does not consume owner-review capacity.**

**★ CORRECTED IN R1 — R0 contained a real contradiction between this section and `§E13.3`.** This section required a conformance result *before* owner review; the functional map places conformance *after* it. Both are needed, and they are **two different moments**: a **machine preflight** before scarce human attention is spent, evaluating what is decidable against the pinned base; and a **final conformance evaluation** after decisions, exceptions, conditions and the final revision set are known. Only the second can be current, because the accepted set does not exist until the decisions do. **A preflight pass is admission evidence and never satisfies the conformance gate.** At a thousand machine-authored proposals a day, a queue that accepts everything syntactically valid is a denial-of-service weapon aimed at authority holders.

Required interfaces: proof-carrying admission · machine-decidable rejection before human review · deduplication and coalescing · consequence/risk classification · WIP limits and backpressure · owner-capacity awareness · deadlines and legal clocks · reserved emergency capacity · reviewer-independence requirements · compatible change waves · dead-letter and escalation. **The final scheduling algorithm is not settled here.**

**`G1-FIND-55` — the scarce input is decorrelated judgment, and it does not come in one currency.** Twenty agents on the same model, corpus and policy are one opinion at twenty times the cost; a queue that counts them as twenty inputs gets *more* wrong as it scales. But the entry receipt's *"independence budget with three substitutable forms"* is too loose to author, and the relief review was right to hold it: **soak time is exposure evidence, not judgment; machine verification cannot replace a legally or professionally non-delegable authority; human review cannot make a machine-decidable hard failure disappear without an attributed exception.** Corrected to **policy-declared independence requirements and evidence channels by consequence class**, with plurality of channel preserved and no single independence score.

**And this binds to an existing accepted row rather than to a new scheduler.** `AB-04` rejected the universal two-implementation mandate and replaced it with an **independence-proof ladder** — second independent implementation · independent parser/validator · independently authored conformance suite · alternate consumer · portability/fork drill · standards-native comparison — under the explicit rule that **evidence strength rises with consequence and lock-in risk**. That row is already `adopted_narrowed`, already routed to the **G1 conformance model**, and already marked `blocks G1`. **The admission model and the conformance model are the same ladder viewed from opposite ends**, and Output 2 should say so rather than building a second scheduler beside it. Full independence assessment remains **Output 6's**. `[CAN→6]`

**Sampling audits a class of decisions made under a pre-authorized policy. A sampled-but-unreviewed change is not approved.**

## §E13.15 — The self-application guard

**This loop governs the resources that define this loop** — the manifest contract, authority and decision policy, conformance rules, the protected integration path, boot routing, and this operations contract itself. `AB-08` was a failure **inside the self-governing subset**: the artifacts that went stale were the ones the process uses to know its own state.

**No new "constitutional document kind" is minted.** The guard binds to Output 1's existing resource facets and placement policy, Build OS protected surfaces, and the authority grammar.

> **Core invariant: a change may not become valid by using the successor rules it proposes to justify itself.**

For any resource governing the architecture-change process:

1. the change is evaluated under the **currently effective predecessor ruleset**;
2. the proposing operation **cannot be its own sole validator, approver or independent proof**;
3. successor rules activate **prospectively only**, after acceptance, landing and verification;
4. predecessor rules remain **resolvable** for historical reconstruction and recovery;
5. **any reduction in review, proof, authority or protection is itself a high-consequence change** requiring explicitly stronger review;
6. emergency or degraded operation may not waive non-derogable rights, independently borne duties, or the evidence needed to review the emergency afterwards;
7. where changing a validator or its policy could change the verdict, **old and new validators are cross-run**.

Relation semantics, lifecycle and conformance detail remain Outputs 3, 4 and 6; the executable guard is G2. **The boundary is Output 2's.** `[CAN→3/4/6 · G2]`

## §E13.16 — Agent continuity and contribution lineage

The live fixture is this arc: a veteran authoring context exhausted, a relief reviewer entering, a veteran reviewer continuing, a fresh authoring context taking over, a fresh reviewer taking the review seat — **all over one branch, one carrier, one work package.** Chat labels are not durable identities.

**Non-collapsing objects** — names remain subject to governing vocabulary; the distinctions are mandatory: work package/lane · architecture operation · **seat/function** · **holder binding** (who occupies a seat, in what scope, over what effective interval) · principal · actor · **runtime profile** · run · attempt · thread/conversation · contribution · grant · handoff receipt · decision receipt · integration receipt · evidence capture.

**★ CORRECTED IN R1 — R0 made an actor a new identity every time it started a run, which breaks the exact continuity this section exists to establish.** Two separate things: **stable actor identity** is `operator/project namespace + actor` and persists across every run; the **contribution attribution coordinate** is `actor + runtime-profile revision + run + attempt` and locates one piece of work. **The display name is not the identity**; two actors may carry the same label in different namespaces without ambiguity, and the same actor under a new runtime profile is the same actor with a different attribution coordinate.

**Replacement semantics.** The work package is unchanged · the prior run and attempt end, suspend or lose their claim · **authority does not pass through prose or pasted context** · a handoff records exact durable state and unresolved obligations · the successor receives a **new holder binding and grant** · a new run and attempt begin · contributions remain attributed to the producing actor, run and attempt · overlap is **explicit concurrency**, never accidental double possession · replacement does not duplicate work · **independence is assessed per claim, never inferred from differing model names** (`§E12.2`) · the prior transcript may inform the successor and **does not become governing truth**.

**`G1-FIND-56` — the attribution and rights relations that must not collapse into one.** *(No count stated: the set was extended once already at `§E13.27.7`, and a count in a heading is a derived value.)*

| Fact | What it answers | Grounded in |
|---|---|---|
| **Contribution lineage** | Who produced what | The event history |
| **Credit** | Who is recognized | Organizational or program **policy** |
| **Accountable commitment** | Who accepted or committed the change | An authority-bearing decision receipt |
| **Scoped rights** | Who may do what with it | A right attaches to an **exact resource · right type or bundle · holder · scope · effective interval** — never a scalar "ownership" (`§E13.27.7`) |
| **Custody** | Who physically holds a copy or fixation | Possession, which confers no meaning and no authority |
| **Legal / professional liability** | Who answers for it externally | **Law, contract, duty, role and facts — outside OMNI** |

The entry receipt said liability is *"a policy over the contribution graph."* That goes too far. **OMNI records and resolves liability bases; it does not invent liability because an agent authored more tokens or touched more files.** The distinction matters most exactly where it is easiest to lose: when the actor is a replaceable process, fusing contribution with liability makes the process the principal, which is both false and unusable.

**A participant set, holder set, thread or contribution set does not thereby become a principal, collective body or acceptance authority.** Under **`AB-15` / `INV-17`** (`adopted_narrowed`, routed to G1): an **atomic statement** has exactly **one issuing principal** and may carry many actors, signers, witnesses, reviewers, endorsements and dissents; a **collective act** exists only as a **composite object with its own identity**, a named collective body or process, a **decision rule**, and constituent statements that remain **independently attributable** — optionally issued by a recognised collective principal where one legally exists. Absent that constitution, the constituent acts retain their own principal, actor, seat and decision lineage. **Roster size, agreement, tally and duration confer no force of their own.**

**A solo actor is one occupied authoring function in one work package** — not a degenerate trifecta. The current three-function collaboration pattern is a **bootstrap operating profile** (`§E11.E`, where its participants are recorded), and the constitutional content is the set of non-collapsible functions — operator intent and consequential acceptance · repository-native construction · independent falsification · affected semantic authority · bounded landing · proof — **not the number three.** The profile grows when a change requires a function that cannot be collapsed and shrinks when it does not.

**`architecture_steward` separation, stated as a prohibition because the seat is where every ambiguity gravitates.** These functions remain separable even when one person currently holds several: completeness assessment · semantic ownership · exception authorization · residual-risk acceptance · cross-cutting acceptance · integration · independent verification. One holder may occupy several **only** under the applicable static/dynamic separation-of-duty policy, and **each exercised function is separately receipted.** A steward who assesses completeness, waives missing ownership, grants the exception, accepts the residual risk, approves the shared resource, integrates it and judges the correction adequate **is a sovereign architect** regardless of what the model calls them.

## §E13.17 — Reasoning evidence: the addressability seam

**Live estate finding, and it corrects what I was about to propose.** I intended to route captured build reasoning to the `build_evidence/` lane. **The lane stub explicitly forbids it** — *"this is NOT a shadow Build OS ledger. Internal build findings, agent build logs, codebase discoveries, test/eval results go to their existing homes."* That lane is for **externally-sourced** build technique. Verified before writing; recorded because the near-miss is the point.

**What the estate actually has.** **★ R1 — the count is now a typed quotation rather than a hand-maintained number, which is the only fix consistent with `§E13.7`.** Enumerated set: `.cursor/plans/*verbatim*.md` **as of `ee1fa6e05b4313e49aa361e75a2dea11b491de18`** — **14 files, 2.3 MB, spanning arc segments `C4.2B` · `C4.2C` · `C4.6` · `INS-G0` · `INS-G1A` · `FAI PRE-0` · `FAI G0`.** The glob is the source; the number is a quotation pinned to a revision and **must not be restated anywhere without that pin.** All are **catalogued**, all passported with a consistent contract — `Authority: NONE. Preservation confers no authority (GRD-036)` · `verbatim_preserved · immutable_once_pasted · never_default_loaded` · *"source, not authority; where this thread and a committed carrier differ, the carrier controls"* — and a **custody-vs-authorship split** already separating who holds the record from who authored the content. And `v4_C4_0_depth_preservation_protocol.md` is **`active`**: a standing anti-flattening rule forbidding authoring any section from a routing pointer alone.

**`G1-FIND-57` — reasoning loss is an addressability problem, not a storage problem, and the estate proves it.** `C4.0`'s mechanic for ingested evidence is *registry row → downstream homes → reopen the cited source spans*. It works because the **EVRUN concept registries index into the sources.** Internally-produced reasoning has the sources and **no index**. The verbatims are correctly `never_default_loaded`, which makes them write-only in practice: reconstructing the `AB-08` rationale in this pass cost a full independent run to recover facts that were **known in the thread where the change was made**. Someone already hit this and hand-patched it once — `v4_INS_G0_kickoff_subagent_verbatim_index_2026-08-08.md` exists because one arc needed an index badly enough to build one manually.

**The precise honest statement, tempered from the entry receipt's overclaim:** OMNI has a repeated, passported verbatim-preservation practice and an **active read-side depth discipline**. It does **not** have a general write-side capture, span-addressing or decision-linked reasoning-index contract. Level one (canonical state) and level three (full transcript) exist; **level two does not.**

**The seam, and it must not become another hand-maintained registry.** Addressable reasoning references attach to **existing** objects — decisions (`03`), conflicts (`05`), guardrails (`06`), open-review items (`08`), findings, acceptance receipts — and **the index is generated from those references.** A decision receipt references the rationale that produced it; the rationale unit records claim, basis, alternatives rejected, residual uncertainty, and a pointer to the verbatim span. **The addressable unit is the decision or the rejected alternative, not the session.** `never_default_loaded` survives: the answer to a million tokens of reasoning is never to boot the next agent on it, but to make it **findable from the decision it explains.**

**Two constraints on the captured object.** The ordinary captured material is **visible** rationale, source anchors, rejected alternatives, uncertainty, decisions, tool and action traces, and contribution outputs. **Do not design OMNI around guaranteed access to a model's private hidden chain of thought** — it is not reliably available, not stable across vendors, and not a substrate to build accountability on. And the rationale reference is a **relation over existing decision, conflict, guardrail, finding and review identities — not a second parallel canon.** `[CAN→G2 · generation · Evidence Plane · lane placement]`

**`G1-FIND-58` — retention is governed by an accountability-and-evidence horizon, and contestability is one input rather than the whole rule.** *Ephemeral cognition does not imply ephemeral consequence.* A transcript may be unretained, excluded from personalization, deleted under policy, minimally retained or under legal hold — while a consequential act still owes a durable minimal record: who or what acted, under which principal and grant, which inputs and versions mattered, what decision or effect occurred, what evidence proves it, what authority accepted it. The horizon composes **contestability · rights and duties · consequence · safety · legal and contractual retention · auditability · reproducibility · privacy minimization · legal hold.** Build and care share the **grammar** (principal · actor · runtime profile · run · attempt · conversation · contribution · grant · decision · evidence · handoff · lineage) and **must not share the retention, privacy or authority profile** — a care thread cannot inherit build retention policy. `[CAN→Care · Evidence Plane · not settled here]`

## §E13.18 — Effectiveness is jointly derived

The entry receipt said effectiveness is asserted by the receiving scope *"never by the origin."* **Overcorrection, withdrawn.**

| Side | Owns |
|---|---|
| **Origin** | Source revision · issuer-side validity and effectivity · withdrawal · supersession |
| **Receiving scope** | Local admission · activation · profile applicability · local variation |

**`effective(scope, effective_as_of, recorded_as_of, mode)` is derived from both** (`§E13.10`; `§E13.5` for the mode). And a federation member's non-admission is **not automatically drift** — but neither is it automatically *"fully conforming."* It resolves to a named posture: `supported_older_version · authorized_variation · transition_skew · incompatible · unsupported · security_revoked · attestation_withdrawn`.

**Sovereignty prevents forced adoption. It does not compel OMNI to attest that every declined revision remains conforming.** The distinction is load-bearing in both directions: without it, drift metrics report every sovereign operator as broken and the correction queue fills with work that must never be done; with it overstated, OMNI would vouch for a security-revoked revision because someone declined to leave it.

**`landed` ≠ `effective` ≠ `observed` ≠ `conforming` ≠ `reconciled`**, and at fleet scale there is no single moment when *the* architecture is uniformly deployed.

## §E13.20 — The 2026 floor and the 2030/2035 frontier

Mechanism probes, never authority (`§3.9.2`, `M-207` — take the mechanism, not its ownership or economic assumptions).

| Mechanism | 2026 adapter (probe) | Durable invariant | Frontier residue |
|---|---|---|---|
| Operation history | Durable-workflow event history; attempts distinct from results | Causal, bitemporal, replayable, no-hindsight | **Portable and replayable without the runtime that wrote it** |
| Staleness | Observed-generation markers on reconciled status | Invalidation is a **predicate** over pinned constituents | Machine readers demand it inline; a stale answer becomes a liability event |
| Integration | Merge queue against a moving base | **Semantic** collision is decided above Git | Collisions are between *intents*; Git may not be the carrier |
| Decision lineage | Policy-decision logs with bundle revision | A decision carries its exact authority and policy basis | Cross-operator decisions verifiable by a party that **distrusts the issuer** |
| Artifact provenance | Build provenance binding artifact to builder and inputs | Derivations are content-addressed over pinned inputs | **The snapshot becomes an externally consumed attestation** |
| Review | Human review queues | **Independence, not volume,** is the scarce input | Policy-declared independence channels by consequence class (`AB-04` ladder) |
| Authorship | Humans propose | **Proposal is never commitment** | Proposals arrive proof-carrying; humans govern envelopes and exceptions |
| Agent identity | Session and chat identity | **Work identity survives actor replacement** | **★ R1:** replacement is routine; thread identity becomes **non-authoritative and non-durable as work identity — not irrelevant.** R0 said *irrelevant*, contradicting `§E13.17`, where the thread is the evidence carrier and reasoning-span locator the whole seam depends on |
| Degraded operation | Block or bypass | Named degraded authority + typed verification debt | Debt discharge becomes a governed capacity constraint |
| Care-time authority | Internal RBAC check | Right context · actor · patient · moment · authority | **Counterparty agents query and verify OMNI's architecture at care time** |

**Two frontier claims stated plainly.** First: by 2035 the Effective Architecture Snapshot stops being an internal artifact. A payer's agent, a regulator's agent and a patient's own agent will consult it to decide whether to trust an OMNI assertion, which means it must be **verifiable by a party that does not trust OMNI** — a materially higher bar than *immutable and machine-generated*, and one only content-addressed derivation over pinned inputs can meet. This is the architecture-layer form of `G-18`: the home is GCE and its build-facing contract does not exist. Second: the human bottleneck becomes an architectural object with capacity, expertise, interruption cost and emergency reserve — governed like compute. **Neither is reachable on an identity and history model weaker than the 2026 floor, which is exactly what V1's single `change_id` was.** The candidate was constitutionally ahead of current practice and operationally behind it, which is the dangerous combination.

Not *"the surfaces were fixed."* **Every current Output-2 assertion of a derived value must either be the owning source, resolve to it, or be a pinned quotation.** A future checker must flag both `AO-SELF-1` episodes — `ee1fa6e` and `eb8a2da` — and pass the corrected head, **differing only in being right**, which is the negative-control standard `ledger:289` sets for `AB-08`. **Four failed episodes over one defect class, by one author, under four independent reviews.** Each pass was more careful than the last; each still shipped restated derived values, and the pass that changed the *method* still shipped them. **The conclusion is not that the author must try harder — it is that a hand-restated derived value is unmaintainable at any level of diligence, which is precisely what `§E13.7` asserts and what G2 must mechanize.**

**The acceptance test for this fixture is a reader test, not a count.** Can a fresh reader who was not present state the current law — one operation, three levels, where authority originates, how effects separate from commitments, what a successor receives — **without reconstructing which revision overruled which?** A marker tally answers a different and easier question, which is why it kept getting published in place of the real one.

## §E13.27 — Dynamic assignment, run context, and the one law behind three patches *(added R2)*

`§E13.16` answers *what happens when actor B replaces actor A.* The operator's live question is **earlier and broader**: who decides B should exist, whether A continues, whether C is added, what each may see, and when one is retired. That is **dynamic execution staffing and context allocation**, and the proposal did not have it.

### §E13.27.1 — The unifying law, which makes three separate patches one rule

**`G1-FIND-61`.** R0 let a controller manufacture a substantive obligation; R1 closed that and left submission manufacturing owner duties; both are instances of a third case the operator surfaced — context pressure, cost, latency or error rate being treated as authority to change the roster. **One law:**

> **Evidence alone exercises no normative authority.** A substantive obligation, authority or assignment **resolves to a pre-existing authoritative basis** — law, contract, right, policy, role, prior commitment or attributed decision — **and enters OMNI's governed operation through its rightful gate.** An accepted deterministic policy may automate **recognition or instantiation**; it does not manufacture the underlying authority.

**The second clause is load-bearing and an earlier formulation got it backwards.** Saying *"admission is always a governed act"* without it reads as *the duty does not exist until OMNI admits it* — which is false for every obligation arising from law, contract, patient rights, professional duty, a prior commitment, a court or regulator, or operator sovereignty. **OMNI recognises, resolves, instantiates and records such duties; it does not originate them.** Making admission the origin of duty would install OMNI's intake function as a hidden sovereign over exactly the authorities the substrate exists to protect — and an unadmitted patient right would read as no right at all.

| Instance | Evidence | Rightful gate | Pre-existing basis it resolves to |
|---|---|---|---|
| Detection | Observation, candidate finding | Evidence admission → substantive obligation (`§E13.13`) | The rule, contract or duty the defect violates |
| Proposal | Submission event, preflight result | Proposal admission → decision obligations (`§E13.3`) | The owners' standing authority over the affected resources |
| Staffing | Context health, budget, error rate, uncertainty, unavailability | **Assignment decision** → holder binding (`§E13.26.2`) | The appointment authority's standing power to assign |

**There is therefore no constitutional "100-pitch rule."** A universal threshold that automatically retires an actor would make a metric into an authority — the exact collapse this law forbids. **The trigger is evidence; the assignment, continuation or retirement is a decision** by a named appointment authority or an accepted policy for that class. Existing candidate percentages in the Agent Runtime capture remain **candidate values to test, not architecture law**.

### §E13.27.2 — The layers that must not collapse

Final names and schemas remain open. The distinctions do not.

| Layer | Question |
|---|---|
| Function / seat definition | What functions exist; what may and may not each do |
| **Work-package function requirement** | Which functions does *this* operation require; which must remain independent or exclusive |
| **Actor qualification / authority constraint** | Who is eligible to hold it |
| Assignment / **holder binding with effective interval** | Who occupies it now, in what scope, over what interval |
| **Execution topology** | Which actors are serial, concurrent, parent/child, peer, reviewer, successor, integrator |
| Run and attempt | What bounded execution is occurring *(Agent Runtime)* |
| **Mission Context / run-context draw** | What did this run receive, and why |
| Claim / lease | Who currently possesses which writable surface *(Build OS)* |
| Contribution graph | Who produced what |
| Decision / acceptance | Who exercised authority |
| Credit · ownership/custody · liability | Who is recognized, who holds rights, who answers externally |

**A work package may declare, where material:** required and optional functions · which functions may be co-held · separation-of-duty and independence requirements · exclusive-writer and protected-surface constraints · allowable concurrency or overlap · token, cost, time and latency budgets · proof and termination requirements.

**Holder-binding behaviour needs equivalents for** appoint · augment · planned overlap · handoff · suspend · retire · replace · revoke · expire · vacant. **Not frozen as enum values here.**

**Retirement or replacement** ends or changes the binding **prospectively** · ends, suspends or transfers the claim · creates a new run/attempt for the successor · **preserves every prior contribution, decision and evidence item** · transfers no authority through prose or context · **does not imply the prior actor failed** · and does not make principals fungible.

**Replaceability is scoped, and this is the load-bearing limit.** Actors and runs are routinely replaceable; function holders are replaceable under assignment policy. **Principals, patients, rights holders, professional authorities and independently liable owners are not interchangeable because a new actor became available** — they change only through explicit succession, delegation or appointment. A new actor can inherit an authoring run; it cannot inherit operator authority by receiving the operator's context.

**Generic scheduler, worker, queue, fairness, backpressure and actor-selection mechanics bind to Agent Runtime and Build OS and are NOT minted here.** They are named open runtime-formulation debt in the Agent Runtime capture, tracked as `G-02` (seat transfer/suspension) and the owed Agent Work Protocol *Context Health + Controlled Handoff* amendment. **Output 2 states how architecture work uses them; it does not build a shadow home.** `[CAN→Agent Runtime · Build OS · G-02]`

**`G1-FIND-62` — independence is a claim-scoped, multi-axis *profile*; no single axis establishes or refutes it.** `§E12.2` scoped independence to a claim; this extends it to the axes on which a claim can be independent at all.

| Axis | Independent when | Current bootstrap profile — **self-assessed, not independently established** |
|---|---|---|
| **Appointment** | Author and reviewer are not appointed by the same authority | **Dependent** — one appointer |
| **Organizational / economic** | No shared employer, funder or commercial interest | **Dependent** |
| **Context / information** | Reviewer inputs are not selected by the reviewed party or a shared router | **Dependent** — a shared router selects both |
| **Evidence / source** | Conclusions rest on separately obtained sources | **Partially separated** — the reviewer reads the live repository directly, over overlapping material |
| **Method / model** | Different reasoning path, model or technique | **Unknown.** Differing model identity does **not** establish it: both receive overlapping sources, work under related instructions, and may share training-distribution and reasoning biases that no brand difference detects |
| **Decision / appeal** | The verdict is not revocable at the reviewed party's discretion, and appeal is defined | **Limited** — the verdict blocks; the delegator may withdraw the delegation; no appeal path is defined |
| **Conflict of interest** | No stake in the reviewed outcome | **Not independently established** — absence of an *observed* conflict is not an assessment |

**A concrete independence assessment is itself a claim and must carry:** the claim being assessed · the assessor · the evidence · the scope · the effective interval · unresolved dependencies · the posture per axis. **The values above are self-assessed by the reviewed party and are therefore evidence, not an assessment** — which is the same law applied to itself. Final values and assurance minima are **Output 6 / `§G1-AUTH`**.

**Common appointment establishes dependence on the appointment axis and proves nothing about the others; differing model identity proves almost nothing on its own.** Two consequences worth stating plainly. First, **the axes are not equally purchasable** — method/model independence is cheap, appointment independence requires a different appointer, and economic independence may be unobtainable inside one organization at all, which means **some assurance claims cannot be satisfied internally at any level of diligence and require an external party.** Second, the present trifecta is **valuable internal independent falsification carrying material appointment, routing and economic dependence** — it is not external independent assurance and must never be presented as such. **Required minima per axis are policy-declared by consequence class.** `[CAN→6 · independence assessment · §G1-AUTH · appointment and recusal authority]`

### §E13.27.3 — The run-context draw, and why it is `AB-08` at runtime

**`G1-FIND-63`.** Each run consumes a **purpose- and authority-scoped context draw** — the existing Agent Runtime *Mission Context* object, not a new one. The draw is a **generated projection**, which means `§E13.9`'s invalidation predicate applies to it and the proposal had never said so.

> **A successor holding a stale draw performs the wrong architecture faithfully.** That is `AB-08` in the runtime plane rather than in prose, and it is the failure mode the operator's manual relay currently prevents by hand.

The draw is therefore: **not** canonical architecture · **not** work identity · **not** a grant · **not** authority · **not** a substitute for its sources · **not** automatically durable knowledge. A successor normally receives a **newly assembled current** draw, never a cloned prior conversation.

**The receipt requires a bounded envelope, because "everything not loaded" cannot be enumerated.** An earlier draft asked for the exclusion set without bounding the candidate set, which makes the receipt either a lie about completeness or an attempt to list the universe. Seven fields, and the first and sixth are what make the rest truthful:

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| **Declared selection universe** | The bounded candidate set actually considered — routing graph, corpus, search result set, work packet |
| **Required set** | What policy says must be present for this purpose and consequence class |
| **Included set** | Exact source identities and **revisions** delivered |
| **Known material exclusions** | Deliberately withheld · deferred · rejected · unavailable — each with reason and policy basis |
| **Selection mechanism** | Router, query, policy and runtime-profile revision |
| **Unknown / unsearched posture** | What lies **outside** the declared envelope, stated as unknown rather than implied absent |
| **Reopen and challenge path** | How the recipient contests coverage or retrieves original material |

Plus: target function and actor · purpose and authority scope · context/token/cost budget · the relay or distillation applied · freshness and invalidation posture.

### §E13.27.4 — Staged disclosure is a distinct relationship, and the live fixture is this pass

The operator withheld a large speculative context packet from the authoring run, routed it to the independent review function first, and forwarded a distilled result. **That is not delegation** — and it is not one thing at all. **Three orthogonal axes, which an earlier draft fused into a single six-row table:**

**Axis 1 — work and authority relationship.** *Who is accountable, who holds custody, whose authority applies.*

| Relationship | Authority and custody |
|---|---|
| **Delegation / subagent** | Parent assigns a bounded objective; parent stays accountable; child has narrower authority |
| **Peer consultation** | One function asks another for analysis; neither owns the other |
| **Independent review** | Reviewer returns evidence or a blocking decision under a review grant |
| **Handoff / succession** | The holder of work or function changes; durable state and obligations transfer |
| **Augmentation** | A contributor joins while the original holder remains |

**Axis 2 — communication and delivery mode.** *How the payload travels.* Directed delivery · **broadcast** · relay (verbatim · excerpt · summary · synthesis · translation).

**Axis 3 — context-selection and disclosure policy.** *What the recipient is given.* Full-envelope disclosure · **staged disclosure** · blinded · sequenced · embargoed.

**These compose freely, which is why fusing them fails.** Staged disclosure can apply to a delegation, a review, a consultation or a broadcast; broadcast is a delivery mode and not a relationship; independent review can be blinded or fully disclosed. **The schema belongs to Agent Runtime and the Evidence Plane; Output 2 establishes only the distinction and the binding.**

**What staged disclosure actually buys, stated narrowly.** It can preserve **blinding and information separation** and **reduce anchoring**. It does **not** create independence — the same router that stages the disclosure is a **context-axis dependency** (`G1-FIND-62`), so a claim that staging *produces* independence contradicts the profile directly. **Its risks are structural and must be receipted:** the router can shape the author by selective disclosure · required evidence can be withheld · the distillation can flatten the source · **and the recipient cannot verify the exclusion set.** I am the author in this fixture and cannot verify what was withheld from me, which is why the receipt fields at `§E13.26.3` are obligations rather than conveniences. **A relay is evidence and never supersedes its source**, and disclosure may never withhold evidence a required authority holder needs in order to decide lawfully.

### §E13.27.5 — The orthogonal breakpoint law

**`G1-FIND-64`. Work state ⊥ holder-assignment state ⊥ run state ⊥ claim state ⊥ context-generation state. A change in one never silently advances another.** Five independent clocks — and the operator's live question, *"are we at a breakpoint for the work, or for the agent, or for both?"*, is answerable **only** because they are separable. Fuse any two and running out of context starts to look like finishing a phase.

All of these are therefore legitimate and individually representable: same work, same holder, **new run** after compaction · same work, **new holder**, newly assembled context · same holder, **new work phase** · a specialist **added** while the author remains · a reviewer added **without** transferring custody · an actor **retired** while the work stays open · a **work checkpoint** reached while the actor continues · work **split** into child packages with nobody retired · **runtime profile changed** under an attributed assignment decision.

**`solo` · `dyad` · `trifecta` · `quadfecta` are derived views over active holder bindings — never stored operating modes.** A stored mode is a duplicated projection of the binding set that drifts the moment a holder changes, and it hard-codes a participant count into a substrate whose point is that the roster varies. An operation never *becomes* a trifecta; three functions happen to be occupied.

**What an agent may and may not do about its own staffing.** It **may** report and recommend — context exhaustion approaching, a specialist is needed, fresh independent review is warranted, this work should split, this runtime profile suits the next phase poorly. It **may not** appoint its own reviewer, grant itself authority, or certify its own independence, unless an accepted policy explicitly authorizes that bounded action. This is `G1-FIND-61` turned on the actor's own roster: **the agent's report is evidence; the assignment is a decision by the appointment authority.**

**Lineage means work, function and decision lineage — not a vendor or model brand.** *"Keep the Opus lineage going"* is architecturally about preserving the authoring function's continuity and its decision history, not the model behind it. **Model continuity and model diversity are both legitimate assignment objectives recorded with the decision, and neither is universally superior** — continuity preserves accumulated framing, diversity buys method independence (`G1-FIND-62`), and which the work needs depends on whether the live risk is drift or blind spots.

### §E13.27.6 — The conversation and relay graph

The operator's question is exact: *does each seat's thread get stored, and does a successor really want to read two near-identical transcripts?* **No — and merging them would destroy the only part that matters.** Identical relayed text is not two truths; **the divergence between what each seat did with it is the signal.**

| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Content unit / payload** | The exact words, artifact, excerpt or structured packet — **one logical identity, content-addressed.** This is an identity and lineage rule, **never a physical storage rule**: tenant isolation, encryption domains, sovereign custody, legal hold and offline operation may all legitimately require duplicated bytes, and **logical deduplication never collapses retention, custody, privacy or authority across those boundaries** |
| **Communication event** | Who authored or uttered that payload, when, in which thread |
| **Delivery event** | Which actor or thread **received** it, and when |
| **Relay / transformation event** | Verbatim copy · excerpt · summary · synthesis · translation · reinterpretation, **referencing a named source** |
| **Thread / conversation** | One communication carrier with its own participant context |
| **Context-inclusion event** | Which material entered a particular **run-context draw** (`§E13.27.3`) |
| **Contribution relation** | Which finding, decision, objection or artifact the event contributed to |

**This answers the operator's case directly.** One operator message delivered to two seats is **one content unit with two delivery events**, not two stored bodies. Each thread keeps its own local conversation. A reviewer's verdict relayed verbatim to the author is a **relay event referencing the source**, not a duplicate of it. **Relay order need not be round-robin** — `1, 1, 2, 3, 1, 4` is an ordinary delivery sequence and the graph carries it with no notion of turns.

**The successor receives a minimum-sufficient continuity projection**, generated over this graph and therefore invalidatable and pinned (`G1-FIND-63`). It contains: **controlling current baseline · exact current work state · unresolved obligations · decisions accepted and rejected · material divergence among contributors and reviewers · unique contributions not represented in the baseline · source references · selection coverage, exclusions and uncertainty.**

**Divergence is one compression dimension of that packet, not the packet.** A successor given only *how two seats differed* would miss the conclusion both relied on, the shared unchallenged assumption, and the current branch state. Full transcripts remain conditional forensic evidence and never default boot (`§E13.17`).

**Source precedence for continuity, and it must obey the working-packet law.** An earlier formulation said *point the successor at a committed artifact rather than a generated prompt*, which is wrong and contradicts binding law: `operator_context_and_collaboration_model.md` §2.5 states that files identified as the working packet control the immediate object **including local, uncommitted or pasted files**, and that no collaborator may reject a supplied packet merely because the repository has not caught up. The correct rule:

> **Accepted committed artifacts control accepted state. A newer, explicitly identified local or uncommitted working packet controls the active object of work and is not discarded because Git lags. A prompt, relay or summary is transport and evidence — never authority — and must pin the sources and revisions it represents.**

So a generated handoff prompt is sometimes **necessary**: when the active delta is uncommitted, when unresolved reasoning or assignments live outside the artifact, or when the successor needs the current packet rather than the last landed state. What it may never do is **silently replace** either source. And every continuity claim carries its state label — `current working packet · local/uncommitted · committed · verified-against-repo · not-yet-verified` (§2.5).

**Human contributions are first-class, and that is not a claim about authority.** They must not be lost — a one-line operator objection can redirect an arc, and a model weighting by volume would systematically under-record the operator. But **human status alone confers no general authority**: the operator may be right, wrong, drifting, hyperfocused or deliberately probing.

**And some authority classes are restricted to qualified humans.** Certain rights, duties, eligibility conditions and authority classes are reserved **by law, consent, representation, professional qualification or policy** to a patient, a natural person, a licensed professional, a legal representative or another qualified human. **Force derives from the specific authoritative basis, eligible holder, act, scope, purpose, interval and current validity — never from generic humanity and never from contribution volume.** While such a restriction applies, **an agent does not acquire the restricted authority through capability, context access, superior reasoning, or an appointment beyond the delegable scope.**

The same actor's messages therefore carry different force depending on the **act performed and the seat exercised under a valid basis**: speculation is evidence, an instruction is an assignment act, an objection is evidence or a blocking act depending on the grant, and an acceptance is a commitment. **This is `G1-FIND-61`'s fourth instance and the operator is not exempt from it** — a human's evidence no more manufactures authority than a detector's does. Treating operator input as *"assumed context"* loses the act; treating it as automatically authoritative invents one.

**Final schema and retention bind to Agent Runtime and the Evidence Plane. No Output-2 subsystem is minted.** `[CAN→Agent Runtime · Evidence Plane · G2]`

### §E13.27.7 — The realization chain, run as a falsifier

The operator's music framing was tested against the model as a **falsifier, not vocabulary**. No musical term enters OMNI. The links, tested honestly — the result is stated after the table rather than in a headline, because a headline ratio over a table is a derived value:

| Link | Covered? |
|---|---|
| logical work ≠ representation/carrier | **Yes** — Output-1 resource ⟂ revision ⟂ descriptor; carrier digest ⟂ logical-revision digest (`§E12.7.3`) |
| representation ≠ authorized profile transformation | **Routed** — Output 5 |
| authorized transformation ≠ **role-scoped execution projection** | **GAP — candidate resolution proposed at `§E13.27.3`; closes on Output-2 acceptance** |
| original realization/fixation ≠ **later independent realization of the same work** | **GAP — candidate resolution proposed below** |
| projection ≠ run/realization | **Yes** — Agent Runtime run/attempt |
| run ≠ observation/trace | **Yes** — `§E13.13`, post-R1 |
| observation ≠ accepted publication | **Yes** — candidate vs published (`§E13.9`) |
| publication ≠ local realization | **Yes** — joint effectiveness, local admission (`§E13.18`) |
| realization ≠ derivative/fork | **Yes** — `§E12.7.3` mirror/alias/fork/derivative/successor row |
| audience response ≠ commit authority | **Yes** — observation is evidence, never authority |

**Result, stated precisely rather than as a headline ratio:** of the ten links, **seven already held outright**, **one is routed** to Output 5 rather than held, and **two were genuine gaps** — the role-scoped execution projection, and later independent realization. *(An earlier draft said "eight of nine already held," which both miscounted the table and conflated held-outright with routed. A reviewer separately claimed the table held eight rows; it held nine, and now ten. Recorded because accuracy runs in both directions.)*

**`G1-FIND-65` — the second gap is the one the re-recording case exposes, and it is not a restatement of content-equality-does-not-imply-identity.** A re-recording of the same songs realizes **the same underlying work** with different performers, equipment, production and provenance; it may be sonically near-identical; it has a **different fixation identity**, different custody and different economic rights; and it is **not a derivative of the prior master.** The chain previously jumped from *realization* to *derivative/fork* and marked the distinction covered. It is not covered:

> **underlying work ⊥ original realization/fixation ⊥ later *independent* realization/fixation ⊥ release/publication ⊥ carrier/distribution copy.** A later realization may implement the same underlying work **without deriving from** the earlier realization, and may become the preferred release for a scope **without erasing** the prior realization or its rights.

**The OMNI consequence is the vendor-removal case, and that is why this is architecture rather than analogy.** Two implementations may realize the same accepted contract; **a replacement implementation may be independently produced rather than derived from the vendor implementation**; and behavioural similarity merges **neither** resource identity, provenance, custody, rights, semantic authority **nor** liability. This is the same independence structure `AB-04`'s proof ladder already governs — *second independent implementation · independently authored conformance suite · alternate consumer · portability drill* — and it is what the substrate-independence row of `§E13.20` actually requires in order to be provable.

**Requirement on the operations loop:** a change operation must be able to **create a new realization of an existing logical work** rather than mutating or superseding the prior realization. Final relation semantics (`realizes` / `embodies` / equivalent) route to **Output 3**; preferred-or-effective release resolution routes to **Output 5**.

**Rights must be scoped, not scalar.** An earlier draft added *"economic/IP ownership"* as one relation, which is itself a collapse. Any right attaches to: **an exact resource · a right type or bundle · a holder · a scope · an effective interval.** Ownership of an underlying work, ownership of a particular fixation, custody of a copy, distribution authority and recognition credit are **not one relation**. The non-collapsing set is `contribution lineage ⟂ credit ⟂ scoped rights ⟂ custody ⟂ semantic authority ⟂ accountable commitment ⟂ legal/professional liability`, and `§E13.16` states it — **not restated as a count here.** A performer's contribution confers no commit authority over the work; a custodian of a fixation owns no meaning. **Output 2 designs no IP or licensing policy;** substantive rights route to enterprise/legal architecture. `[CAN→3 · relation semantics · 5 · release resolution · enterprise/legal]`

### §E13.27.8 — Boundary for this section

**Establishes:** the distinctions and composition interfaces above. **Does not settle:** the scheduler or roster optimizer · context-health thresholds · actor-selection policy · model/provider routing · cost allocation · the final roster schema · workforce law · IP and licensing policy · Evidence Plane implementation · clinical retention · the context-router implementation. **No new artifact, no new output, no new lane, and the trifecta is not canonized as N=3** (`§E11.E`).

# §E14 — Output 3 · ARCHITECTURE GRAPH SEMANTICS — six governed objects, no sovereign graph
