| R32 | active relation surviving endpoint cessation without required revalidation | the relation's current force | `§E14.7.4` | terminate current force; preserve history |
| R33 | vacancy resolved by silent steward or operator fallback | authority resolution | `vacancy ≠ implied authority` | reject; block per decision condition |
| R34 | ownership edge from a P4/P5 resource to canonical truth | the edge | `T0-15`, `D0THES-DEC-033` | reject — while **`owns_definition` remains permitted, read as the exact scoped semantic-authority / definition-ownership fact over a definition resource** (`§E9.3`), **never as generic `owns` returning through a side door** (`R42`) |
| R35 | historically consequential object **lacks the temporal fields** the requested mode requires | the **query**, not the object | `§E14.5` matrix | fail — *unanswerable*, never a confident answer |
| R36 | foreign assertion whose governing **predicate semantics fail `predicate_semantics_usable`** for the receiving scope and declared temporal query — no base usability, no usable one-hop mapping, no authorized mapping path | effective edge | `§E14.3.2`–`§E14.3.4` | exclude as **unadmitted semantics** — **distinct from `R23`**, which is instance-level usability |
| R37 | a **mapping treated as identity or equality** | the mapping claim | `§E14.3.1` rule 4 | reject |
| R38 | a **stale or superseded mapping** used without required revalidation | effective edge | `§E14.3.1` rule 5 · `§E14.2.1` | exclude as stale |
| R39 | an object's **structural field reified as an assertion** to bypass its authority, lifecycle or validation | the assertion | `§E14.1.3` | reject |
| R40 | `conflicts_with` **substituted for a governed `ConflictRecord`** | the conflict handling | `§E14.1.3` consequence 2 | reject — detection is not adjudication |
| R41 | cross-owner **constraint** declared without a resolved affected-authority set | the constraint | `§E14.4.1` | block — never default to a steward |

## §E15.0 — Purpose, what Output 4 is not, assignment and force

**The purpose, stated once and governing every section below** `[KND]`:

> **Output 4 supplies the shared semantic contract for architecture change and evolution across separately owned OMNI lifecycles. It defines the minimum distinctions, attribution, composition, failure, correction and historical-coherence rules those lifecycles must preserve. It owns neither the native lifecycles nor their deciding authorities.**

**It exists so that Care, Platform, Accountability, Commerce, Federation, operators and execution mechanisms do not each invent an incompatible meaning for *changed*, *approved*, *landed*, *effective*, *reverted*, *recalled* or *resolved*.** Consumption cases are evidence that the grammar is adequate or inadequate. **They are not the purpose, and no consumption case — including architecture's application of this grammar to itself — is the durable object of this output.**

> **★ THE COMPOSITION THESIS — the center, and the thing distinctions alone do not supply** `[KND]`. **One architecture change is one correlated change case over a revision-pinned, scope-qualified set of separately owned lifecycle facts.**
>
> **"Change case" is a reading name for accepted Output-2's correlated architecture operation, at change grain. It is not a new object family.** Accepted Output 2 already establishes it: *"a governed architecture change is one correlated architecture operation — a durable intent carrying a correlation identity, an authority basis and a causal history, and carrying **no atomicity claim whatsoever**"*, identified by `operation_id` (= `change_id`), **immutable, not an idempotency key for anything, and owned by Architecture Operations** `[INH §E13.2`, `§E13.4]`. **Output 4 owns the composition contract over it. It does not own the correlation fact, and it is not the operation's owner.**
>
> **The case is not the manifest, the resource revision, the assessment, the decision, the release, the disclosure, the admission, the deployment, the activation, the effect, or the observation.**
>
> **★ And the ownership split is stated exactly, because *"the case owns correlation"* is one sentence away from a central correlation graph that re-sources every native causal fact** `[KND]`:
>
> - **Architecture Operations owns the correlated-operation identity, and the attributed declaration that named facts participate under it** `[INH §E13.4]`;
> - **each native fact owner retains ownership of its own event, decision, effect, evidence, obligation and causal assertions** `[INH §E13.5`, `§E13.7]` — architecture history **references** them causally and **never re-sources** them;
> - **a case graph or case view is a generated projection over attributed correlation and causal references**, owning no underlying causal truth `[INH T0-15`, `DEC-033`, `§E14.1.2]`;
> - **Output 4 owns only the semantic composition contract** — how those references compose, and nothing they contain;
> - **and holder coincidence merges no fact and no authority function** (`§E15.1`), however few principals presently hold them.
>
> **★ And the ownership kinds are ENUMERATED, not counted — the rows are the enumeration and no total is maintained** (`F-06`) `[CAN`, class D]. **The set is open**; these are the kinds the retained laws require, and a governing source may establish another: the **owning domain** holds the **authoritative state** · the **principal or legal entity** retains the underlying **right or duty** · the **actor or delegated agent** accepts **custody of the next work** within granted scope · the **committer** is the actor-plus-domain that makes a consequential state **authoritative** · and the **substrate** holds only the **continuity invariant** (`§E15.2.3`). **`Authoritative state` is deliberately not `truth`** — it is the owner's authoritative record, correctable later, and calling it truth is how a domain record becomes unchallengeable. **Guard: a non-human agent may accept delegated execution custody and does not thereby acquire independent professional authority or legal personhood** `[INH DEC-035]`.
>
> *The failure this forestalls is concrete: a "case graph" that starts as a convenience for reading correlation, becomes the place correlation is edited, and ends as the authority on what caused what — at which point every native owner's causal assertion has been quietly appropriated by a projection.*
>
> **And correlation merges nothing** `[KND]`: **not identity, not ownership, not authority basis, not scope, not clocks, not currentness, not history, not outcome.** *This is the sentence the rest of `§E15` depends on. A catalog of `X ≠ Y` laws tells a reader what must not fuse; it does not tell them how one real change composes across many owners without fusing — and an implementer handed only the catalog will supply the missing composition object themselves, which is the monolith every one of those laws exists to prevent.*
>
> **★ WHERE OUTPUT 4 SITS RELATIVE TO THE ESTATE'S CANDIDATE INTENT-TO-CONSEQUENCE CONSTITUTION** `[CAN]`. The estate carries a candidate **cross-domain constitution governing whether and how consequential intent may become authoritative state or real-world effect — or reach an honest non-action terminal** — through admissibility, domain-owned commitment, accepted custody, honest continuity, selective reopening, remedy where owed, and bounded proof. **It is broader than Output 4 and it owns no domain state, is not a universal custodian, and allocates no legal liability.**
>
> > **Output 4 is that constitution's ARCHITECTURE-CHANGE COMPILATION: the shared change grammar separately owned native lifecycles must preserve when architecture change may create, alter, prevent, migrate, expose, supersede, compensate or leave unresolved consequential state and effect.**
>
> **Output 4 neither owns nor renames it, and creates no such object, service, domain, plane, controller or universal lifecycle.** *That one relationship prevents both failures at once: the candidate evaporating because no gate would adopt it, and the candidate centralizing because an output treated it as a thing to build.* **Conceptually central; operationally distributed.** *The word `compilation` is the candidate's own build law and not a coinage: the candidate is compiled into contracts, policies, gates, guards, projections, proofs and evaluations, and is never deployed as one central service.*
>
> **★ AND THE CANDIDATE IS ITSELF SUBORDINATE AND ITSELF UNGATED — both facts were missing here, and each carries an obligation onto this output** `[KND`, class D]. **① The candidate does not sit at the top.** Its own terminus places it **UNDER** the estate's inherited **care-first, patient-rights, recommendation-integrity and anti-capture commitments**: *it governs consequential transition; it does not define OMNI's ends* — *a determination can be perfectly traceable and still unjust.* **The relationship is three-part, not two**: **the care-first mission supplies the ends** · **the estate's named alignment composition (`Polaris`) keeps movement aligned toward them and owns no objects and no enforcement of its own** · **the candidate governs the conditions under which consequential change may occur.** **② The candidate's freeze covered more than its definition.** It froze the eight invariants, the responsibility model, the legal guard — **and also its NEIGHBOUR BOUNDARIES and its RATIFICATION GATES.** **Its first ratification gate is a clean doctrine dedup against `Polaris`, `REV-184`, `CNS`, `OFC`, `§C`, Care, Commerce, Identity, Consent, Evidence, Accountability and Agent Runtime — and that gate is UNPASSED.**
>
> **What follows for Output 4, stated as an obligation rather than a reassurance** `[KND]`. **Adopting propositions from an ungated candidate at this output's own force is legitimate — a destination is not trapped at its source's force — but it INHERITS the source's undischarged dedup duty at change grain, and this output does not discharge it.** *Named neighbours this output does not reconcile against: **`Polaris`**, which the candidate's own source says **enters at the admissibility invariant** — precisely where `§E15.2.3` clause 6 routes substantive admissibility to Care and `§G1-AUTH` and names no alignment composition at all; and **`REV-184`**, which owns the lifecycle of forming, deferring, revising and reopening a consequential decision that `§E15.4.1`, `§E15.4.3` and `§E15.9` all compose over.* **Neither is contradicted here and neither is reconciled here.** **The source additionally records admissibility as the LEAST-PROVEN of its invariants and the one that keeps the set from becoming a well-governed conveyor belt for bad decisions — so the limb this output leans on hardest is the limb its source trusts least.** **★ THE DEDUP IS NOW DISCHARGED FOR THE TWO NEIGHBOURS THIS OUTPUT LEFT UNRECONCILED, AND NEITHER IS A DUPLICATE** `[CAN`, class D]. **Both were read at their controlling surfaces — Polaris in full, `REV-184` at its canonical `§0` output, which is SIGNED OFF and CLOSED as a review row and carries seven named spine-grade lines.** **The five are different KINDS of thing and the boundary is stated as a composition, not a hierarchy:**

> **The care-first mission supplies the ENDS** — patient care is the end and nothing here is. · **`Polaris` is the named ALIGNMENT / TRUST / PROOF COMPOSITION** that keeps movement aligned toward those ends; **it owns no objects and enforces nothing itself** — the owners it names enforce, at every seam. · **`REV-184` owns the DECIDE LAYER** — one actor-agnostic governed resolution lifecycle at the authority gate between Sense and Act, resolving a raised signal or candidate into a stance, with **CNS** owning the resolution record as process-state-not-truth, **RBAC** owning the authority and blast-radius gate, the owning domain owning commit, and **`OFC` — Ordered Fulfillment / Care Obligations** owning obligations arising *from* a stance. **Its scope is TWO SEPARABLE PRIMITIVES and it is stated exactly, because both loose readings are dangerous** `[INH]`: `OFC` is **`canonical` for the Act-loop lifecycle substrate at `draft_for_ratification`**, and it owns the **lifecycle STATE** of *things ordered or fulfilled* (**`fulfillment_order`**) and *things owed or due* (**`care_obligation`** — due, recall, retest, refill, monitoring, exception), **delegating all truth to the rightful domains.** **It does NOT own the originating stance or resolution · the obligation's basis · clinical, commercial, legal or professional truth · release AUTHORITY merely because it records release STATE · every obligation, task, reminder or duty in the estate · or universal work custody.** *(Recorded against two opposite errors, both live: an earlier revision here said `OFC` owned the *"fulfillment-slice state only"*, which **erased the separately governed `care_obligation` primitive**; and a proposed expansion of `OFC` to an obligation-continuity name was checked against the estate and is **false** — minting a name for a real canonical domain would be promotion-by-vocabulary in the clause written to prevent it. **The generic reading is one step from making Fulfillment the universal obligation custodian this section rejects; the narrow reading loses the primitive that carries what is still owed.**)* · **The Reactor candidate supplies the INTENT-TO-CONSEQUENCE invariants** governing whether and how consequential intent may become authoritative state or effect. · **Output 4 is the ARCHITECTURE-CHANGE COMPILATION** — how one change composes across separately owned facts over time, and what must not fuse.

**Why these do not collide** `[KND]`. **`REV-184`'s subject is a DECISION; Output 4's subject is a CORRELATED CHANGE.** *One resolves a single raised signal at a gate; the other composes many owners' facts across time and scope.* **Output 4 mints no stance vocabulary and re-authors no resolution** — its `decided` predicate (`§E15.3`) **references a `REV-184` resolution as the authoring source of the decision it composes over**, exactly as `§E15.4.1` already requires that the assessment never be the approval artifact. **And `Polaris` does not collide with either**, because it is a *read over distributed enforcement* rather than an enforcing layer: where `§E15.2.3` clause 6 routes substantive admissibility to the owning domain and `§G1-AUTH`, **`Polaris` is the name for that composition of owners at the admissibility seam — which is exactly where the Reactor candidate's own source says alignment enters.** **No object, service, plane, controller, lifecycle or authority is created by this reconciliation, and no concept is quarantined.**

**Three laws Output 4 INHERITS rather than restates, now that their owner is named** `[INH]`: **non-action-as-commit** — an attributed determination of *no change* is a positive result, which `§E15.4.4`'s recorded-null already states at change grain and `REV-184` owns generally · **outcome-reads-the-original-context-and-never-rewrites-it**, which is `§E15.11`'s no-hindsight rule sharing one law with `REV-184`'s decision layer · and **world-model honesty** — *a predicted or believed state is a candidate, not truth*, which `§E15.4.1` already carries as simulated-never-becomes-observed.

> **★ And ONE law Output 4 is MISSING, found by this dedup and referenced rather than restated** `[CAN]`. **`REV-184` bounds authority by `trust_horizon`: *authorized autonomy ≤ trusted horizon*, shortened by staleness, uncertainty, irreversibility and blast radius.** **Output 4 carries the OBSERVATION horizon (`§E15.4.1`) and the grant-and-policy currency test (`acceptance_currently_usable`) — and neither is this.** *Those ask whether consequence can be seen in time, and whether a grant still stands. This asks whether the world-model the authority rests on is still trustworthy enough to support the autonomy being exercised — and it can fail while the grant is perfectly valid and the observation perfectly timely.* **At change grain, and stated precisely because the loose form is dangerous: a still-valid grant is NOT SUFFICIENT where the context or resolution basis the consequential transition rests on has passed its applicable trust horizon. The transition is re-resolved, narrowed, escalated or blocked under the rightful owner's policy — and expiry of trusted context does not by itself revoke, rewrite or expire the underlying grant.** ***Four facts that must not collapse, and they are four facts rather than four fields:*** **whether the grant still exists and is in scope** · **whether the decision context is still within its trusted horizon** · **whether a prior resolution may still be relied on for this purpose and scope** · and **whether this actor may perform this consequential transition now.** *Three conflations are forbidden by that split: **stale context is not revoked authority** · **an unusable prior decision is not an erased one** · and **required re-resolution is not universal human review** — a standing authorized policy may re-resolve automatically.* **The law, the horizon's computation and the degraded-mode threshold are `REV-184`'s, `RBAC`'s and `CNS`'s — Output 4 states only that the change grammar must reference the horizon and may not assume authority survives context decay.** **Recorded as an inherited reference, not as new Output-4 law.**

## §E15.1 — The distinguishability contract

**This is a distinguishability and fact-ownership requirement. It is not an inventory, a population, a census or a near-schema, and it is not an ownership claim** `[KND]`. Output 4 does not reauthor the subjects below; it states which of them must remain **separately identifiable and separately attributable** so that the laws in `§E15.3`–`§E15.15` can be stated at all, and it names who owns each fact so this output cannot quietly become that owner.

**The splitting rule, which governs membership and replaces any count** `[KND]`. **Two lifecycle-bearing facts are separate whenever any of these differ: logical identity · authoritative owner · transition authority · clocks · admissible transitions · failure physics · termination or survival behaviour · conformance consequence.** *A row bearing two owners or two clocks is a fusion wearing a slash.*

**Six posture statements that make this a contract rather than a list** `[KND]`:

1. **The set is open.** It is a declared-open minimum. **No total is asserted anywhere and none is maintained** (`F-06`) — a maintained count is a derived value that drifts the moment the set grows and carries no architectural information.
2. **No census is claimed.** Coverage is a claim with a declared posture, never an asserted complete set (`§E15.4.4`); claiming completeness would be the population-versus-sample defect `G1-FIND-74` records.
3. **Each fact has exactly one authoritative owner in scope** `[INH §E13.7]`. **And holder coincidence does not collapse facts** `[KND]`: **one holder may occupy more than one owner or authority position where governing policy permits, and that coincidence merges neither the facts, their authority bases, their evidence requirements, their challenge paths, their scopes nor their clocks.** *A sole operator holding six positions still holds six facts; the day a second principal takes one of them, nothing has to be re-decomposed. Collapsing on coincidence is how a small estate builds a model that cannot grow, and how a party ends up adjudicating its own liability by accident rather than by design.* **No holder object, role taxonomy or authority model is minted here** — the positions are named where the facts are named, and who holds them is `§G1-AUTH`'s and the owning domains'.
4. **Several facts inside one end-to-end episode routinely belong to different owners.** One change touching one release, one operator and one patient produces facts owned by the publisher, the receiving scope, the deploying authority, the emitting boundary, the affected domain and the recognizing authority — and no one of them owns the episode.
5. **A cross-cutting change grammar does not own the subjects it joins.** Output 4 supplies the grammar; the owner column is the enumeration.
6. **These are not interchangeable kinds of thing, and treating them as one frame is a category error** `[KND]`: a **truth-owning domain**, a **cross-cutting capability that composes distributed truth and owns none of it**, a **projection or surface** (`T0-15`, `D0THES-DEC-033`), an **operating loop**, an **execution mechanism**, a **sovereignty boundary condition**, and a **scenario over the whole set** are six different kinds. A grammar law can be consumed unchanged by one, require specialization by another, and be structurally inapplicable to a third.

**The minimum distinctions the retained laws require** `[KND]` — each one exists because a law below cannot be stated if it collapses:

| Must remain distinguishable | Authoritative owner of the fact, in scope | Why it cannot collapse |
|---|---|---|
| the **proposed change artifact revision** ⟂ the **architecture resource revision** it would alter | Architecture Governance for the proposal; the resource's rightful owner or steward for the resource `[INH Output 1]` | submission commits no architecture `[INH §E13.3]`; supersession is a typed transaction over the resource, not an edit of the proposal `[INH §E7.1.2]` |
| the **assessment** ⟂ the **decision** | the assessment issuer for that fact and scope; the deciding authority for the decision | an assessment is a required input to approval and is never the approval artifact (`§E15.4.1`) |
| **prospective** ⟂ **simulated** ⟂ **observed** consequence | assessment issuer · the executing simulation's owner · the observer, admitted separately `[INH §E13.13]` | simulated evidence must never become a claimed real-world outcome, and pre-commitment evidence must never be discarded as mere opinion (`§E15.4.1`) |
| the **authority grant** ⟂ the **decision** it supports | RBAC / authority history for the grant; the deciding authority for the decision | grant expiry may block a later effect and erases no decision `[INH §E13.10]`; architecture history references grants causally and never re-sources them `[INH §E13.5]` |
| **publication** ⟂ **local admission** ⟂ **adoption** ⟂ **deployment realization** ⟂ **activation** ⟂ **effective use** ⟂ **support claim** ⟂ **conformance claim** | the publisher · the receiving namespace or principal · the adopting principal · **`environment` / `deployment_target` authority, which is `OPEN` in the estate and stated as unresolved rather than filled** · the claim issuer · Output 6 for what conformance means | the whole of `§E15.7`; each is a real operational position and none implies the next |
| the **external commitment** ⟂ the **emitted effect** ⟂ the **acknowledgement or demonstrated reliance** ⟂ the **domain-typed consequence** | the accountable principal · the emitting boundary (GCE) · the observer · the affected domain owner | `§E15.6` and `§E15.9`; a commitment is not its effect `[INH §E13.2]`, and reliance is an observation about another party rather than an act by OMNI |
| the **obligation** and its **separately held positions** | no single owner — see `§E15.9.1` | collapsing them is what lets a party adjudicate its own liability |
| **migration execution** ⟂ **coexistence envelope** | the migration owner · the envelope owner named at opening | partial application is first-class; a difference inside a valid envelope is coexistence and the same difference outside one is drift (`§E15.8`) |
| the **compatibility determination**, carrying **both its dimension and its interaction relation** | the determining authority or authorized generator | a single verdict cannot represent compatibility impact — see the two-axis law below |
| the **observation event** ⟂ its **admission** | the observer · the admitting authority `[INH §E13.13]` | an observation survives even when evidence admission fails `[INH G1-FIND-59]`; unreachable or unknown is not observed `[INH §E13.10]` |
| the **original act** ⟂ the **correction, reversal, compensation, amendment or retraction** | each act's own acting owner | a correction is a new linked act and never an overwrite (`§E15.9`) `[INH §E13.4]` |
| **historical reconstruction** ⟂ **execution replay** ⟂ **forked continuation** | history owners · the attempt owner (Agent Runtime) · the branch's own new work | a reconstruction that can re-fire an effect turns a historical query into a second real act (`§E15.11`) |

> **Fleet posture, effective-architecture snapshots and resolved desired state are generated projections over admitted owner-scoped facts. They are not distinctions in this contract, because minting one would give a projection an owner of truth** `[INH T0-15`, `DEC-033`, `§E13.9]`. Any materialization of them is read-only, generation-stamped, invalidatable, and prohibited as an input authority unless re-derived from its owning facts. **Generated is nonetheless not ownerless** `[INH §E14.1.2]`: a generator-contract owner, an authorized generator, a publication authority, a custodian, pinned inputs and a verification path are all required, and none of them owns the underlying facts.

> **An unresolved owner is recorded as unresolved, and it blocks EXACTLY the transitions that require it** `[KND]`. Where a transition's decision condition requires an authority and none resolves, **`owner_set_complete` is false for that transition** and it fails closed `[INH §E13.10`, `§E13.8]`. **It is not false globally.** The accepted predicate is scoped to *"every authority **required for the consequence class**"* — so an unresolved environment authority blocks environment-authority-requiring transitions and leaves every other transition alone. *Reading it globally would halt the entire deployment plane until the estate settles a matter Output 4 is forbidden to settle.* **Output 4 does not resolve `environment` / `deployment_target` ownership; it refuses to paper over it.**

> **No fact's lifecycle value is readable as another's** `[KND]`. Publication says nothing about admission; admission says nothing about adoption; adoption says nothing about deployment; deployment says nothing about activation; activation says nothing about effective use; none of them says anything about conformance; and a conformance claim says nothing about whether conformance currently holds.

> **★ THE FOUR-WAY DISTINCTION THE COMPOSITION CONTRACT RESTS ON** `[KND]`:
>
> > **correlated change case ⟂ proposal or manifest revision ⟂ participating subject facts ⟂ case-level generated projection**
>
> Four different kinds of thing, four different owners, and the commonest implementation error is fusing any two of them. *The manifest is a document someone submitted; the case is the correlation; the participating facts are the owners' truth; the projection is a generated reading. A surface that shows one screen has not thereby made them one object.*
>
> **Membership laws** `[CAN]`:
>
> - **one case may span many subjects and many scopes**, and **one subject or scope may participate in several cases at once** — a resource under two concurrent proposals, an operator receiving three releases, a patient affected by a protocol change and a formulary change;
> - **participation is revision-pinned and causally attributable**;
> - **temporal proximity, shared files, graph adjacency, common authorship and being downstream do NOT establish membership** — those are search heuristics, and treating a search result as a member is how a case silently acquires facts nobody correlated;
> - **a newly discovered affected subject may update impact coverage and invalidate a prior assessment's usability without rewriting the prior case history** (`§E15.4.1`, `§E15.4.4`).
>
> **★ And participation is TEMPORAL — it resolves under the ACCEPTED temporal mode, and this mints no second temporal model** `[CAN]`. **Case participation and affected-set projection resolve under the declared temporal question and both bounds, exactly as accepted Output 2 requires of every other query** `[INH §E13.5]`. The change-grain consequence, stated over the **accepted** question names rather than new ones:
>
> - **`historical_as_now_reconstructed(effective_as_of)`** — later-recorded, earlier-effective participation **may** enter, and later discovery is visible as later discovery;
> - **`known_as_of(recorded_as_of)`** — only participation recorded by that cutoff;
> - **`decision_context_replay`** — only participation the deciding authority could actually have resolved then;
> - **`evaluation_against_the_knowledge_horizon_then`** — only participation available within that horizon.
>
> **A participant discovered later may enter the first answer. It may never silently enter the other three.** *Resolving a decade-old case against today's participation set imports every later-discovered party into a decision that never saw them — the no-hindsight violation committed at correlation grain rather than at fact grain, and the one that would let a 2034 discovery retroactively make a 2028 decision look negligent or look sound.* **The four questions, the no-hindsight rule and the `resolve(...)` interface are accepted Output-2 content, referenced and not restated; no parallel interface, universal field set or temporal engine is minted** (`§E15.11`).
>
> **Corroborated by Care's own participation topology — declared unbounded, dynamic, never fully known, admitting unknown-at-start participants, and carrying join, leave, mute, revoke and re-enter** — class D, conferring no force. **Output 4 states the resolution requirement; the participation record's shape is the owning domain's and G2's.**

> **★ ONE CORRELATED CHANGE MAY BE SIX DIFFERENT SPECIES OF CHANGE AT ONCE, AND NO ONE OF THEM EVIDENCES ANOTHER** `[CAN`, class D]. **A single correlated change may simultaneously implicate: a governed SOURCE's version succession · reconsideration of ADMITTED REUSABLE KNOWLEDGE derived from it · a DOMAIN-OWNED STATE correction · invalidation or regeneration of a COMPILED PROJECTION citing it · reassembly of an ASSEMBLED WORKING CONTEXT that included it · and continuation of an EXECUTION already running on it.** **Six changes, six owners, six sets of failure physics — and *none of them is evidence that any other occurred*.** *A source superseded is not a domain corrected. A projection regenerated is not a truth changed. A knowledge unit reclassified is not a decision revoked. A context reassembled is not a prior context rewritten. An execution continued is not an authorization renewed.* **The estate's own source-and-knowledge constitution separates these classes precisely because one plane, one reservoir or one memory would fuse them** — and it warns in its own text that the classes are **not one ontological kind**, which is why **Output 4 references their separately governed physics and imports no class vocabulary, no plane and no schema.** **What Output 4 owns is only the composition consequence: a correlated change spanning several species is `§E15.2.1` law 3's nonuniformity across SPECIES rather than across scopes, and `§E15.5`'s selective propagation routes to the owners of what actually changed — never to every species because one of them moved.**

> **★ AND THE SEVENTH SPECIES IS THE ONE THIS OUTPUT IS WRITTEN ON: THE ARCHITECTURE PLANE'S OWN DESCRIPTION OF A DOMAIN** `[CAN]`. **Asked directly and unaccounted for until now:** when a domain concept changes and the architecture concept describing it changes, **is that one change or two, are they linked, and do they update together?** Output 2's self-application carry (`§E13.15`, Output-4 leg) is still open, so the answer is composed here from accepted law rather than left to the next reader to re-derive.
>
> **First: which of two things the architecture surface actually is, because the failure is not knowing.**
>
> | The architecture surface is… | Then it… | And a domain change… |
> |---|---|---|
> | a **description** of a domain's own truth — a catalog entry, a graph node, an impact projection, a generated snapshot | **owns no truth, must remain re-derivable from the domain's authoritative facts, and carries a reference to them** `[INH T0-15`, `DEC-033`, and the creation-time back-pointer at `§E15.11]` | **invalidates it.** It is not a separate decision; it is a derived thing that must re-derive or be marked stale |
> | an **independent architecture assertion** — a constraint, a contract clause, a policy, a required treatment the architecture imposes | **is its own change subject with its own owner, gate and lifecycle** | **does not change it.** It changes only through its own authority |
>
> **A surface that reads like the first and is stored like the second is the drift case**, and it is the exact shape both planes report as healthy: the domain moves, the description does not, and nothing is wrong on either side's own terms. *That is why the back-pointer is required at creation rather than audited later.*
>
> **Second: the direction is asymmetric and never symmetric.** The architecture plane may **require** things of a domain and may **describe** a domain. **It may never commit the domain's truth** `[INH` the four-way composition, `§E15.4.5]`. So **a change to the architecture's description of a domain cannot change that domain, while a change to the domain must reach the description.** *Correlating facts confers no authority over them — the same rule the `§E15.0` authority test exists to enforce.*
>
> **Third: therefore they do NOT update together as one transaction, and they are not two unrelated changes either.** They are **one correlated change with separately owned commitments** — accepted Output 2's no-global-atomicity law, realized as local atomicity plus propagation (`§E15.15`). The domain commits on its own authority; the description re-derives or is invalidated; any architecture constraint that must also move is **its own change with its own gate.** **Asking whether they are "linked" has one honest answer: they are correlated and causally ordered, never atomic and never independent.**
>
> **Fourth: architecture change is change, so this grammar applies to itself — and that creates no plane for it.** Maintaining the architecture runs on the **same governed machinery over a different subject**, with each position already owned by an existing home; **no fifth plane, no meta-domain and no external-change god-object.** *Stated at this grain deliberately: an earlier form of this claim mapped the machinery onto a two-loop Sense/Act table with fixed owners per position, and that mapping was **withdrawn as too linear** — architecture sensing also receives production telemetry, fleet divergence, conformance failures, drift, operator reports and security events, so no single boundary is "the Sense side."* **The owned slice is declared against R8's ten operations capabilities above, which is the non-linear form.** **The self-application boundary is where this output must be most careful, because the surface writing the rule is also the surface the rule governs** `[INH §E13.15]`.
>
> **On the comparator question, held to the epistemic discipline** `[INH`, Task-D]: the admissible form is ***"not demonstrated in reviewed public primary sources"***, so no claim is made here about how any incumbent maintains its architecture plane. **The structural point stands without one:** a system holding a single merged model of *the architecture* and *the domain it describes* **cannot express the two rows of the table above** — it has no way to say that a description went stale without saying the truth changed. **That compression is what this section refuses, and refusing it is the cost as well as the differentiator**, because two correlated changes are genuinely more expensive to operate than one merged record.

**Three absence states, and they must not share one token** `[KND]`:

- **evidence-unknown** — a distinction the model carries, with facts missing for it. It reports `unknown`, never clean, and may enter bootstrap or degraded operation under a named authority and the inherited non-derogable floor `[INH §E13.8`, `§E13.11]`.
- **a classification gap** — an affected subject kind the model does not carry at all. **It is not an `unknown` and is not bootstrappable.** You cannot record residual risk against clocks, authority, consequence or survival rules you have not identified, because you do not know what you are risking. It **fails closed for the affected consequence and scope**, and where it is discovered after approval it **invalidates the assessment basis that approval pinned** rather than reporting an unknown.
- **authoritatively established out-of-scope** — **an attributed decision** that the subject kind does not apply here, never an assumption and never a default.

> **★ A compatibility determination is incomplete unless it names BOTH axes** `[CAN]`:
>
> > **A compatibility determination is incomplete unless it identifies both the dimension being judged and the interaction relation or context through which the revisions meet.**
>
> **Axis ① — the dimension.** The **admissible instance set** is one dimension and is not the whole answer. *Adding a required field narrows the admissible instance set while widening the behavioural obligation on producers; widening an enum invalidates no existing instance while breaking consumers that exhaustively matched, or otherwise assumed closure over, the prior value set.* **A change can narrow on one dimension, widen on another and be `incomparable` on a third** — which is why a single scalar hides exactly the disagreement that has to stay visible. **The other dimensions are separate facts with their own owners and this determination duplicates none of them**: semantic meaning is an independently owned assessment record (`§E15.4.2`) carrying accepted Output-3 axis ① `[INH §E14.2.1]`; behavioural requirements, defaults, precedence and consumer compatibility are the affected subject owner's; migration impact is a treatment determination (`§E15.4.2`, `§E15.8`); **conformance and non-loosening judgment is Output 6's and is stated here in no form** (`G1-FIND-23`).
>
> **Axis ② — the interaction relation.** *"Is X compatible with Y"* has a different answer depending on **how X and Y are joined.** **One pair can be compatible under one relation and incompatible under another.** Candidate relations include direct use, local admission, mapping, composition, delegation and an emitted consumer contract — **each already an accepted Output-3 object** (`§E14.3`, `§E14.3.3`, `§E14.4.5`) — **and this list is not a closed enum.** *The final relation vocabulary and the resolution algorithm are Outputs 3 and 5's; conformance and consumer-safety computation are Output 6's.* **Output 4 states only that a determination naming one axis and not the other is incomplete, and mints no relation taxonomy.**
>
> **Reference the owning result; add no mandatory field set** (`G1-FIND-106`). Restating another owner's dimension as a field here would be `D0CKPT-GRD-003` committed inside its own repair — two predicates built at G2 from one fact, arriving through vocabulary.

## §E15.2 — The minimal reference algebra, and what it may never impose

**A shared reference layer exists so separately owned lifecycle contracts can be joined, compared and reconstructed. It is a reference algebra, not a record shape, and it imposes no schema** `[KND]`. **Record *families* are not tables**: how any of this is physicalized, indexed or stored is G2's, and a reader who turns a family into a table has made an implementation choice this output does not make.

**★ FIRST: WHICH TRANSITIONS THE CONSEQUENTIAL-TRANSITION LAWS GOVERN — the grammar's own activation predicate, stated here because it was relied on throughout and defined nowhere** `[CAN]`. `§E15.2.3` clause 5's proof requirement, clause 6's admissibility ordering and `§E15.14`'s decidability-of-refusal requirement all trigger on a transition being **consequential**, and no section said what that meant. *A cold implementer cannot apply this grammar without it and would supply the missing predicate — the supply-the-missing-object failure `§E15.0` exists to prevent.*

> **A transition is CONSEQUENTIAL when, under its declared scope and on a PROSPECTIVE basis, it can establish, alter, terminate, invalidate or require action upon a SEPARATELY GOVERNED position — an authoritative fact · a duty or custody position · an authority, admissibility or applicability position · a support, compatibility or claim position · an affected party's standing under that party's own domain's determination · or an externally relied-upon state — OR when it can cross a commitment frontier.**
>
> **A position is SEPARATELY GOVERNED where its identity, authoritative owner, authority basis, scope, clock, challenge path, survival rule or consequence semantics are independently attributable. HOLDER COINCIDENCE NEVER COLLAPSES SEPARATE GOVERNANCE.**

***An earlier revision of this predicate said "a position held by anyone other than its own actor." That was wrong and is corrected*** `[KND]`. **It contradicted `§E15.1`'s own holder-coincidence law** — *one holder may occupy more than one owner or authority position, and that coincidence merges neither the facts, their authority bases, their evidence requirements, their challenge paths, their scopes nor their clocks.* **Under the actor wording, a sole operator holding six positions could move all six as one non-consequential internal act, and the grammar would switch off precisely where `§E15.1` says the facts stay separate.** *The estate's own decomposition is the reason: `actor ≠ principal ≠ owner ≠ authority holder ≠ committer ≠ affected party`, and a boundary drawn at the actor collapses five of those. **The boundary is separate governance, never separate people.***

**This is a CONSOLIDATION of two laws this output already carried separately, not a new one** `[KND]`. The **external limb is `§E15.6`**, which already defines the frontier as *the point past which the world outside the changing subject has been affected in a way the subject cannot unilaterally undo*, and `§E15.4.1` already makes the frontier record **the** discriminator for whether an execution touched the world. The **internal limb is `§E15.1`**'s one-authoritative-owner-per-fact-in-scope, which already makes *reaching a fact you do not own* the bright line. ***Output 4 held both halves and never joined them into the trigger the rest of the section runs on.*** *That is why the gap was invisible: nothing was missing from the parts, only from their composition — which is the same defect at meta-grain that `§E15.2.1` exists to prevent at change grain.*

**Four properties, each excluding a wrong reading** `[KND]`: **① it is a REACH test, not a MAGNITUDE test** — no threshold is set and none may be inferred; *a one-line change publishing an identifier is consequential and a very large purely internal refactor is not*, and blocking thresholds stay with the applicable consequence policy (`§E15.4.4`), this predicate deciding only which transitions that policy is asked about · **② it is PROSPECTIVE and per-transition** — decided on what the transition **can** reach, before it runs; **a transition is not reclassified because an effect turned out badly, nor excused because one failed to materialize**, since deciding it afterwards lets outcome determine obligation, which `§E15.11` forbids at decision grain and this forbids at activation grain · **③ an unresolved determination stays TYPED UNRESOLVED and receives consequential-grade protective handling — it is NOT recorded as a positive `consequential` fact** — the transition is protected as if consequential and any step requiring a resolved determination blocks, **while the model continues to say it does not know**; *recording uncertainty as a positive classification is the recorded-null defect `§E15.4.4` forbids and the absence-manufactures-a-result defect `§E15.3` forbids, committed by the clause that activates them* · **④ it activates obligations and confers nothing** — being consequential imposes admissibility, authority resolution, proof and decidable refusal, and **grants no authority to perform the transition** (`§E15.5`) · **⑤ the HISTORICAL determination and the CURRENT determination are separate facts** — later evidence may supersede the current classification, enlarge the affected set or require a new assessment, and **may never rewrite what was determined then or the basis it was determined on**; this is `accepted_historically ⟂ acceptance_currently_usable` at classification grain `[INH §E13.10]` · **⑥ it activates the grammar and does NOT set enforcement depth** — *which* shared laws activate, and to what evidentiary and review depth, is `§E15.2.3` clause 5a's declared activation keyed to consequence class and effect envelope. **Consequentiality is the gate; risk-adaptive activation is what happens past it, and collapsing the two would convert every consequential transition into the universal heavyweight workflow clause 5a exists to prevent.**

> **Two limbs of the estate's candidate six-limb version are deliberately NOT lifted** `[KND`, class D]. Its **material-effect limb** — *materially affects a party's rights, care, money, access or commitments* — **is a domain materiality judgment, and Output 4 defines no materiality** (`§E15.7` ④); it enters only as *the affected party's standing **under that party's own domain's determination***. Its **irreversibility limb** — *may produce a hard-to-reverse effect* — **is circular at this grain**: reversibility is derived from change character (`§E15.4.3`), and character is determined by the grammar this predicate activates, so a reversibility test cannot be that grammar's own entry condition. **The frontier limb carries what the irreversibility limb was reaching for, without the circularity.** *Taking the mechanism and not its shape — the discipline this output records against others and has now applied to the source closest to it.*

**Every lifecycle-bearing transition, in every joined contract, resolves the following — as a *semantic* requirement and never as a mandatory column set** `[KND]`:

| Element | Requirement |
|---|---|
| subject identity + subject type | which distinction, which instance, which revision |
| scope | the exact scope the transition governs — operator · deployment · jurisdiction · profile · target · cohort · namespace. **A transition with no declared scope is not evaluable** |
| authoritative owner or issuer | who owns the fact this transition creates |
| **authority-basis reference** | a pointer to the law, contract, right, policy, role, prior commitment or attributed decision the transition rests on. **A reference, never an authority definition** (`§G1-AUTH` owns the ontology). Where the actor is non-human the basis may cite an externally owned **`delegated_authority_envelope`**, which Output 4 neither defines nor owns `[INH DEC-035]`. Three inherited constraints hold: **actor identity, represented principal, capability and commit authority remain distinct** · **no actor inherits the identity of the principal that invoked it** — impersonation is the named anti-pattern, not a shortcut · and **authority is revalidated at the point of consequence**, which is `acceptance_currently_usable`, not a one-time check `[INH §E13.10]`. **★ Sharpened from the runtime's native form** `[CAN`, class D]: *inclusion in an assembled context does NOT preauthorize action*, and **effective permission is an INTERSECTION re-evaluated at EVERY consequential boundary** — tool call, external effect and commit alike — over the **current grant · delegation · execution or tool profile · consent and processing authority · policy · current subject and object state · purpose · scope and jurisdiction · authorized effect envelope · and decision-context usability** (`§E15.0`'s trust horizon). **Presence in the admissible set is NECESSARY, NEVER SUFFICIENT.** *A standing authorized policy may perform that re-evaluation automatically — this requires no human at any boundary — but **the executing runtime never originates the authority it exercises**, and a cached authorization is not a current one.* **Output 4 states that the re-evaluation is owed at each consequential boundary; the intersection's computation, profile bindings and enforcement are Agent Runtime's, RBAC's and `§G1-AUTH`'s** |
| temporal interpretation | which clocks this transition carries, per the object's own physics `[INH §E14.5]` |
| transition / effect identity | the transition's own identity, and where an effect is emitted, the **effect-scoped** idempotency key `[INH §E13.4]` |
| causal + correlation references | parent, cause, correlation to the operation, and the **existing** architecture-semantic event vocabulary `[INH §E13.5]` — **Output 4 mints no second event engine** |
| supersession · migration · correction · compensation links | typed relations to prior and successor acts |
| evidence + uncertainty posture | what is known, what is unknown, what is unreachable, and what is merely claimed |

**Lifecycle condition is a set of concurrently evaluable predicates over separately owned facts. It is never a stored selected value** `[INH §E13.10]`. **The predicates coexist**: `accepted_historically` is permanent while `acceptance_currently_usable` can turn false beside it; `landed` can hold while `effective(...)` does not; several can be true, stale and false simultaneously across different scopes. **The projection is a set or structured view, never a single selected value** — calling these phases is precisely the invitation a surface, schema or vendor adapter needs to collapse them back into one enum.

**What the algebra may never impose** `[KND]` — each prohibition inherits a named accepted or governing source:

- **one universal state enum** — `§E13.10`: the predicates are derived over separately owned facts and are never one writable lifecycle scalar;
- **one universal terminal state** — `§E13.18`: at fleet scale there is no single moment when the architecture is uniformly deployed;
- **one universal bitemporal storage shape** — `§E14.5`: temporal semantics are stated *by object physics*, and stamping one field set across unlike objects is the failure Output 1 spent four passes removing;
- **one universal writer** — `§E13.7` one-authoritative-owner-per-fact-in-scope, and `D0THES-GRD-035`;
- **one global event owner or history owner** — `§E15.11`;
- **one global transition authority** — `§G1-AUTH`, and the canonical four-function composition in which none replaces the others.

> **This shape is inherited, not invented** `[INH]`. `C4.4 §R`'s mechanism template already requires every mechanism to declare its own authority / admission / commit boundary, its lifecycle states and closure, its partial-failure / degraded / unknown / quarantine / retry posture, and its temporal / as-of / correction / supersession / revocation semantics. **Output 4's per-subject contract is that template applied to the change plane.** The coordination seam this creates with `AB-01`/`B-13`'s separate obligation to generalize the same template is recorded at `§E15.17.1` and is not resolved here.

### §E15.2.1 — The change-case composition contract

**This is the composition center. It uses accepted Output-2's correlated operation and creates no object** `[CAN]`. Where the rest of `§E15` states what must not fuse, this states **how one real change composes across many owners without fusing.**

**1 · PARTICIPATION IS ESTABLISHED BY ATTRIBUTED RELATION, NOT BY A MEMBER LIST.** A participating fact joins a case **only through an explicit, revision-pinned, attributed causal or governed-correlation relation.** Accepted Output 2's own words: *its correlation is **declared, not decided*** — no participant is enrolled by proximity, adjacency, shared carrier location, common authorship or downstream position.

> **★ And there is NO canonical member set** `[KND]`. **Any apparent "members of this case" is a generated projection over those attributed relations, for a declared scope and temporal mode, carrying a coverage claim** — exactly like every other case-facing projection (law 5). **No canonical `case_members[]` list is required, and a stored one is a materialized projection subject to law 5, never the source of participation.** *The word "membership" is serviceable prose and a dangerous schema: the moment a member list becomes the thing surfaces write to, participation stops being the owners' attributed relation and becomes whatever is in the list — which is how a correlation convenience acquires the authority to enrol a party that never consented to participate.*

**2 · NATIVE OWNERSHIP SURVIVES MEMBERSHIP.** **The rightful native owner authors each participating fact. The case references it and never re-sources it** `[INH §E13.5`, `§E13.7]`. Membership grants the case a pointer, never a copy and never a write.

**3 · NONUNIFORM OUTCOME IS THE NORMAL CASE, NOT AN INCONSISTENCY.** One case may be accepted and landed centrally while **one receiver admits and adopts · another is unresolved · another refuses · one deployment activates · another stays on a supported older version · one scope crosses an external frontier · another crosses none · a migration remains open elsewhere · a remedy remains owed to one party · and an offline member is unobserved.** **These are not contradictory case states. They are different native facts under one correlation, each current for its own owner and scope.** *The single most common failure is reading nonuniformity as inconsistency and then "fixing" it by picking a winner — which silently overwrites a sovereign fact.*

**4 · ★ TENSION IS REAL AND IT IS NOT NONUNIFORMITY — BUT IT IS ALREADY TYPED ELSEWHERE, AND THIS OUTPUT MINTS NOTHING FOR IT** `[CAN]`. **Two participating facts may be not merely different but incompatible** — an admission pinned to revision *N* while the migration owner declares completion for *N+1*; a live support claim whose conformance evidence has expired; two authorities' determinations that cannot both hold for one scope. **The law is stated as a prohibition on the projection, not as a new object:**

> **A clean case projection is prohibited while any of the following remains unresolved for that projection's declared claim and scope: an accepted Output-3 semantic conflict · an invalidation or stale-basis predicate · an unresolved disagreement between separately authorized owners · or evidence insufficiency for the claim being made.**

**Those are four ALREADY-TYPED conditions with existing owners, not one new condition** `[KND]`. Semantic conflict is **accepted Output 3's first-class conflict resource** with its own resolvability classes; invalidation and stale basis are **accepted Output-2/3 predicates over pinned constituents** requiring no write anywhere; authoritative disagreement blocks with **no hierarchical and no steward fallback** (`§E15.4.5`); evidence insufficiency is a **coverage result** (`§E15.4.4`). **Output 4 mints no universal tension object, no tension lifecycle, no resolver, no precedence algorithm and no second conflict record beside Output 3's.** Resolution routes to **Output 3** for conflict semantics, **Output 5** for precedence and applicability resolution, **Output 6** for evidence sufficiency, and **`§G1-AUTH`** or the affected owner for authoritative disagreement. **What this contract owns is exactly one thing: that an unresolved condition of any of those four kinds forbids a clean projection rather than being averaged into one.** *Corroborated by Clinical Memory's own `unresolved_conflict` state and context-keyed coexistence — class D, conferring no force. **A second conflict model beside Output 3's would be `D0CKPT-GRD-003` at case grain, and this clause exists to make that impossible to write by accident.***

**5 · CASE-LEVEL PROJECTION IS GENERATED, QUALIFIED, AND POWERLESS.** Any case-level progress, posture, completion or summary is **generated over participating facts under a named aggregation policy, a declared scope, a declared temporal mode and an honest coverage claim.** It is **never canonical input authority, and it never advances, closes, certifies or records anything in a native lifecycle.** **Generated is nonetheless not ownerless** `[INH §E14.1.2]` — it carries a generator contract, an authorized generator, a publication authority, a custodian, pinned inputs and a verification path. *The estate reached the same conclusion by withdrawing the opposite one: a composed financing statement owns no source truth and is still not ownerless, because it has a governed record, a version, an execution owner and lineage.*

**6 · THE AFFECTED SET IS OPEN, AND ITS CLOSURE IS A CLAIM.** Affected-subject discovery is a **completeness claim, never an asserted set** `[INH §E13.8]`. Later discovery **adds facts and may invalidate current usability or assessment coverage without rewriting prior history** (`§E15.4.4`, `§E15.11`).

**7 · NEITHER AUTHORITY NOR BURDEN ARRIVES BY COMPOSITION** `[CAN]`. **Membership, correlation, aggregation and case closure confer no authority to act on any participating subject** — the anti-god-object half, and the reason `§E15.3`'s classification seam and `§G1-AUTH` remain external. **And the converse, which is the half a machine-volume substrate cannot omit: membership imposes no obligation on a member absent that member's own pre-existing basis.** *A proposal is cheap for the sender and expensive for every recipient; at machine authoring volume, correlating a party into a case is a way to externalize cost onto them.* **Leverage, influence, burden incidence, default power and material effect are each distinct from authority and none of them may be upgraded into it** — the estate's own decomposition, and the reason a change processor recognizes duties rather than originating them (`§E15.9.1`).

**8 · ★ THE CONTAINER IS OPTIONAL AND ITS LOSS ERASES NOTHING** `[KND]`. **Native facts, obligations and authority-bearing acts are fundamental. Any change-case carrier, document, record or materialization is OPTIONAL, and its failure, loss, absence, corruption or closure erases none of them** — every participating fact remains current for its own owner, every obligation remains owed, and every authority-bearing act remains effective, with or without a container to read them through. **Nothing in this contract makes the case a subject, a state machine, a plane, a service, a domain or an owner of truth**, and **no language anywhere may re-elevate the container.**

> **This is the estate's own discipline, applied to the very section that could violate it** `[class D]`. Accountability holds that *the obligation is fundamental and its case is an optional recipient-scoped container*, with its standing guard being **against language that re-elevates the container.** **Useful case documents and projections are not prohibited — they are expected.** What is prohibited is any of them becoming the truth owner. *Writing a composition center is precisely the act most likely to produce the monolith a composition center exists to prevent, which is why this law is inside the contract rather than only in the boundary.*

### §E15.2.3 — Custody, continuity and the no-orphan invariant

**★ This is CANDIDATE OUTPUT-4 SYNTHESIS. It is NOT inherited law, and the correction matters** `[CAN`, class D]. The estate's intent-to-consequence candidate — adversarially traced through a prescription, payment, pharmacy-acceptance, dispensing, shipment and delivery fan-out with injected partial failure, then independently regraded, then **re-adjudicated in a successor run against an independent incumbent-native adversary** — produced a compact invariant set covering this ground. **Output 4 had re-derived a coarser subset of it without opening it. This section states what was missing, at candidate force.**

> **★ SOURCE FORCE AND DESTINATION FORCE ARE DIFFERENT THINGS, and conflating them is how a serious candidate gets buried forever** `[KND]`. The successor evidence run **self-promotes nothing** and **freezes the candidate's definition against casual prose mutation** — *do not promote it there, do not rename it, do not expand it, do not implement it as a central thing.* **It had the authority to say that about itself. It had no authority to say that no later architecture gate may ever adopt these propositions**, and reading it that way would make every candidate permanently unusable, which is the opposite of how promotion works. **The correct chain:**
>
> > **evidence-run source = nonbinding evidence and frozen candidate doctrine → Output 4's reasoned transfer of a proposition = Output-4 candidate architecture → independent G1 acceptance = accepted G1 proposal semantics → G2 = the durable installed representation.**
>
> **The source stays nonbinding evidence. The destination proposition does not stay trapped at the source's force forever.** ***An earlier revision of this section did both things wrong in opposite directions: it labelled the content "inherited," which was false, and it then said the successor's disposition "governs how this section may speak," which was too broad. Both are withdrawn.*** **The correct label is `adopted from the candidate as Output-4 candidate synthesis` — and whether it becomes accepted law is the acceptance transaction's decision, not this section's and not the source's.** **What the successor genuinely establishes and this output carries forward:** the residual is **material and not repackaging**, and it is a **design-and-conformance residual, not a production or network advantage** — no external party has accepted the semantics or the receipt, and no measured economic, safety, liability or adoption result exists. **The successor adds no invariant and does not prove the candidate's set; Output 4 therefore adopts propositions on its own reasoning, not on the candidate's authority.**

**1 · ★ CUSTODY TRANSFERS ONLY THROUGH EVIDENCED AUTHORIZED ACCEPTANCE — everything else ENDS, RETURNS or EXPOSES A GAP, and assigns responsibility to nobody** `[CAN]`. **Custody is offered and accepted; it is never assigned by fiat, and never by the correlating surface.** The positions that must stay distinguishable: **an offer · verification of the recipient's identity and authority · acceptance · effective time · release · expiry or terminal cessation · and an unfilled gap.**

> ***Only acceptance transfers. Release, expiry, refusal, impossibility and terminal cessation do not*** `[KND]`. They may **end** responsibility, **return** it to the prior holder, or **expose that nobody holds it** — and none of them hands it to a third party. **A local record reading `assigned`, or a transport reading `received`, transfers nothing**: *custody does not transfer because a record says so or a transport acknowledged delivery.* **`§E15.7`'s counterparty chain applies here in full** — command ≠ evidence ≠ authoritative commit, and transport acknowledgement ≠ contractual acceptance ≠ accepted execution custody ≠ execution ≠ consequence. *No acknowledgement, timeout, portal receipt, staff note or adapter callback creates custody by itself.*
>
> **★ And the estate grades this chain more finely than this clause did, on a boundary that is CONTRACTUAL rather than technical** `[CAN`, class D]. ## §E15.2.2 — What a participating lifecycle must expose at the join

**Only what the join actually requires — and this section deliberately adds no second field set** `[KND]`. `§E15.2` already states what every lifecycle-bearing transition resolves, and `§E15.1`'s splitting rule already names admissible transitions, failure physics, survival behaviour and conformance consequence as the properties that make a lifecycle distinct. **Restating them here as a participation schema would rebuild the register this output removed, and would be `D0CKPT-GRD-003` arriving through vocabulary.**

**What is genuinely additional at the join is one thing: the DERIVATION SURFACE** `[CAN]`.

> **A participating lifecycle must declare which of its native facts a shared or case-facing predicate may be derived from, and that declaration is made by the fact's own authoritative owner.**

**Three consequences** `[KND]`: **①** a case-facing predicate may read only what its owners have exposed for derivation — **a projection may not reach into a lifecycle's internals because they happen to be legible**; **②** the declaration is the owner's, so **a lifecycle can participate in a case without surrendering interpretive control over its own facts**; and **③** where a required derivation surface is not declared, the predicate is **not derivable for that member** and the projection reports absence rather than substituting a default (`§E15.4.4`). *This is the same law `§E15.4.5` states for cross-scope reuse — whether my determination travels is a property of my determination — applied to derivation rather than to scope.*

**Everything else a lifecycle exposes is stated where that lifecycle's physics are stated, not here.** Output 4 requires an interface, not a schema, a field set, an enum, a table, a state machine or a storage shape.

## §E15.3 — The admission seam, and why change progress is a projection

**Before anything else: what must be true before this grammar may be applied to a subject at all** `[CAN]`. An earlier form of this output defined a lifecycle for changes without ever stating what admits a subject to it (`G1-FIND-105`). **The seam is stated here as a semantic result Output 4 consumes — not as a classifier Output 4 operates.**

> **★ AND BEFORE THAT: THE CHANGE MAY NEVER HAVE COME THROUGH THIS SEAM AT ALL** `[CAN]`. **Every clause below presumes a subject ARRIVES — is raised, classified, admitted, decided, landed. A large and permanent share of real change does not arrive; it HAPPENS, and the substrate learns late.** `v4_REV184_decision_state_reconciliation.md §0.3` — trifecta-signed-off, seven spine-grade lines — makes *who held the authority gate* a **first-class axis on every resolution**, precisely because the alternative is the fantasy that nothing happens until the substrate authorizes it. **Applied at change grain, the posture is a required property of the change record, not an error state:**
>
> - the substrate's **own gate fired**, and the decision is reconstructable through it;
> - the substrate **proposed and a separate authority committed** — the common case, and not the same as the first;
> - an **external or higher authority committed** it, under its own authority, and the substrate holds an admitted record `[INH `§E15.6` GCE]`;
> - it was **executed first under emergency or break-glass authority**, with the basis recorded **after** the fact;
> - it happened **entirely out of band** — no gate of the substrate's was consulted;
> - **the gate holder is not yet known, pending reconciliation.**
>
> **The last two are the load-bearing ones, and they are postures rather than failures.** *`§E15.12` already models failure, interruption and partial application — an out-of-band change is none of those. It may be entirely correct, fully authorized by its rightful owner, and complete.* What is missing is not correctness but **the substrate's participation**, and the honest record of a change that bypassed the grammar is **not silence and not a defect flag — it is a stated posture plus a reconciliation obligation.**
>
> **Two consequences** `[KND]`. **①** `§E15.3`'s entry predicate and `§E15.14`'s *absence read as permission* both assume the arrival path. **A change with no intake record is therefore ambiguous between three states that must never be collapsed: it never happened · it happened out of band and is unreconciled · it is inside a declared variation declaration and is `configuration`.** Only the second creates an obligation, and nothing in this output previously distinguished them. **②** the reconciliation is **post-hoc and additive** — it records what happened, under whose authority, on what basis, and what the substrate did not know at the time; **it never back-dates the substrate's gate to pretend it fired** `[INH `§E15.9` correction-is-a-new-act]`.
>
> **Why this survives the `§E15.0` denuding tests, stated because the source is a clinical reconciliation and this is exactly where over-transfer happens** `[KND]`. **① failure physics:** strip every patient, OR, transfusion, CPR and signout noun and the failure is intact — *a sovereign operator self-applies a release the publisher never admitted; a security team revokes a certificate out of band; an external standard is already in force before anyone evaluated it; an operator edits production configuration directly.* **② authority:** the axis **removes** an assumed authority rather than granting one — it forbids the substrate from presuming its own gate is universal, which is the same direction as `INV-26` and `GRD-031`. **③ architecture-native:** all four cases above contain no care. **④ mechanism neutrality:** what transfers is **the axis and the non-collapse**; the source's stance taxonomy, `rationale_class`, field set and `proposed→pending→…` state machine are **care-specific or machinery and are NOT imported** — the latter is additionally forbidden by `§E15.2`'s prohibition on a universal state enum.

> **What Output 4 states, and what it must never state** `[KND]`. **Output 4 states the minimum semantic result required before its lifecycle grammar may be applied to a subject, and it consumes and enforces that result's routing or blocking consequence. It does not own the classifier, the method, or the deciding authority.** *Both collapses of that distinction are failures and they run in opposite directions.* **Collapsing toward *"Output 4 classifies"*** makes this output the universal owner of configuration, drift, nonconformance, exception, emergency activity, domain operation and conformance classification — the cross-cutting god-object `D0THES-GRD-035` forbids. **Collapsing toward *"the entry seam is unowned"*** leaves the seam ungoverned, and at machine change volume that means every surface reinvents a classifier and the substrate loses the one seam it exists to hold. **Routed is not ownerless** — the same law `§E14.1.2` states for generated results and `§E15.1` states for every owned fact.

**The minimum semantic result** `[CAN]` — stated as what must **resolve**, semantically, and explicitly **not as a mandated field schema**. Physicalization is G2's; no new object family is minted, and Output 4 does not assert that this result is the same object as any accepted admission decision:

- the **exact subject or revision** the result is about;
- the **exact scope** it covers;
- the **attributed classification outcome**;
- the **determining authority or authorized generator** that produced it;
- the **authority or policy basis** it rests on;

This law applies **only to architecture-owned subjects, or to subjects whose architecture relevance has been established.** Everything else resolves through `§E15.1`'s **authoritatively established out-of-scope** — an attributed decision, never an assumption. *A clinical order deviates from no architecture, and the absence of a declared variation says nothing whatever about it.*

**The routing outcomes that must remain distinguishable, each with a home that already exists** `[CAN]`. **This is an open routing contract, not a closed enum, not a taxonomy and not a new object family.** A result matching none of these resolves to *unresolved classification* rather than to a default:

> **★ Every predicate above is a SHARED OR CASE-FACING PROJECTION over referenced native facts** `[KND]`. `intake_recorded`, `impact_claimed`, `owner_set_complete`, `decided`, `accepted_historically`, `acceptance_currently_usable`, `landed` and `effective(...)` **transition nothing, mutate nothing, close nothing and certify nothing in any native subject.** They are derived under `§E15.2.1` law 5 — named aggregation policy, declared scope, temporal mode, honest coverage — and **a false or absent result is a statement about the derivation, not a state of the subject.** **No universal `case_state` is proposed, and any surface that adds one has re-created the writable lifecycle scalar accepted Output 2 forbids** `[INH §E13.10]`.

**Three laws follow** `[KND]`:

1. **`ChangeManifest.state`, if it exists at all, is an intake convenience, a derived projection or a bounded workflow hint. It may never be the canonical truth from which acceptance, landing, effectiveness, conformance, reconciliation or authority is inferred.** A stored scalar duplicating these facts would be `D0CKPT-GRD-003` committed inside its own fix.
2. **The change functions are a functional map, not an ordering guarantee** `[INH §E13.3]`. Propagation re-enters review; observation runs throughout; correction restarts the shape as a **new** operation with its own correction identity.
3. **Plan `§3.1`'s six-value list — `proposed / reviewed / approved / staged / landed / reverted` — is NOT adopted as canonical.** `§E15.4` records why, and `§E15.5` records what `reverted` actually is.

## §E15.4 — Change characterization: prospective ⟂ simulated ⟂ observed

**`C-03` is CLOSED as a requirement and this output does not reopen it:** irreversible and forward-only change must be representable, and *evolvable* means **reversed where semantically safe — otherwise superseded, compensated, or advanced through explicit forward migration.** What remains open is the vocabulary that happened to close it.

**`G1-FIND-86` — plan `§3.1`'s *"every Change Manifest declares exactly one"* of five labels is not satisfiable on the plan's own terms.** The five labels mix at least five independent facts, and the ordinary healthcare cases satisfy two or three at once: a forward-only public identifier that external consumers already rely on is **both** `forward_only` **and** `externally_committed`; a settled charge that can be credited but not un-charged is **both** `compensatable_not_reversible` **and** `externally_committed`; a schema change to an externally consumed contract is **both** `reversible_with_migration` **and** `externally_committed`. And the same `§3.1` cell places the five labels beside a state list terminating in `reverted`, **which three of the five forbid reaching.** **The labels are a governing obligation to disposition, not a ratified enum, and the plan is not amended here.**

**And a second law the labels hide: a change's character is not one thing measured once.** Some of it is **assessed before the act**. Some of it is **observed after the act**. **A single characterization that mixes them mutates as the operation runs, which retroactively changes what an approval meant** — the no-hindsight violation (`§E15.11`) committed against the approval record, and the reason `accepted_historically` ⟂ `acceptance_currently_usable` exists `[INH §E13.10]`.

### §E15.4.1 — Three provenance positions, never two and never one

| | **Prospective assessment** | **Simulated consequence** | **Observed consequence** |
|---|---|---|---|
| What it is | **several independently attributable records**, each with its own identity and revision, per affected subject and scope | an **execution** producing a result, in which **no external frontier was crossed** | a **derived projection** over execution and observation facts at a declared `as_of` |
| Who authors it | the **assessment issuer** for that fact and scope. **An issuer produces an attributed determination; it does not thereby decide anything** | the owner of the executing simulation, carrying its identity and revision, its input population or scenario set, its declared fidelity and coverage, and its generator lineage `[INH §E14.1.2]` | **generated, and generated is not ownerless** `[INH §E14.1.2]`; the observer owns the observation event, and admission of it is a separate decision `[INH §E13.13]` |
| What it is for | **a required input to approval — NOT the approval artifact.** The approval artifact is the **decision**, authored by the deciding authority | producing consequence evidence **without crossing a frontier** | answering *what has actually happened, as of when, at what coverage* |
| Temporal rule | **the decision references an exact, immutable assessment basis.** Later facts never mutate what was reviewed | recorded with its own times; it is never back-read as a real-world outcome | resolved under `resolve(...)` with mode and both bounds declared |

> **★ The discriminator between simulated and observed is the FRONTIER RECORD, and it is the only one that works** `[CAN]`. **An execution that produced no commitment-frontier event did not touch the world, whatever else it produced** (`§E15.6`). **A simulated-consequence record therefore carries, non-negotiably, the explicit absence of frontier events.**
>
> **Both collapses are live hazards and they run opposite ways** `[KND]`. **Read as observed**, a simulation result becomes a claimed frontier outcome that never happened — **fabricated consequence evidence**, and in care that is the worst available failure. **Read as a prospective assessment**, the estate throws away the strongest pre-commitment evidence it can generate and falls back to a hand-set risk field. **`Simulated evidence never becomes observed consequence.`**
>
> **And the boundary case that matters most: a canary is NOT simulation** `[KND]`. It crosses a **real frontier for a bounded real population**, so it is **observed consequence at reduced scope** and its records are frontier records. A shadow path that consumes real inputs without producing the primary external effect still carries consent, privacy and operational obligations — *"no primary effect" is not "no exposure."*
>
> **What Output 4 does NOT freeze here** `[KND]`: **no simulation taxonomy, no evidence hierarchy, no fidelity scale, no exposure threshold and no ratio.** The operative invariant is **maximize pre-frontier evidence · minimize real-frontier exposure · never substitute simulated evidence for observed consequence** — and the exposure budget varies by risk, reversibility, affected population, authority, novelty, blast radius and clinical or legal consequence. ***A surface that sets a ratio has minted the cutoff that decides what reaches a patient.*** Simulator construction, fidelity assessment, evidence sufficiency and autonomy graduation are **Output 6's, Platform E&V's, CNS evaluation's and G4's**; *whether a simulated result may substitute for an observed one for a given consequence class is a **domain** decision and is never this output's.*

> **★ VISIBILITY, EXPOSURE, CONSEQUENCE AND AUTHORITY ARE FOUR ORTHOGONAL AXES, and the frontier answers only one of them** `[CAN]`. **Prospective ⟂ simulated ⟂ observed describes evidence provenance and whether a frontier was crossed.** It says nothing about **who was exposed, whether they knew, or who authorized the exposure.** A separate **exposure characterization** records **whether a real population or system was exposed · under what visibility or awareness posture · and under what authority basis.**
>
> **The minimal proof that this is a second axis and not a restatement of the first** `[KND]`: **a silent user-impacting release and a disclosed bounded-cohort release can cross the identical frontier, for a comparably sized real population, in the same consequence class — and remain materially different acts.** The frontier record cannot separate them; only the visibility and authority posture can. *An estate that models the frontier alone can prove that the world changed and cannot say whether anyone was told.*
>
> **Four laws follow** `[KND]`:
>
> - **`"Silent" is a visibility posture.
