4. **Partial application is a first-class, recoverable, separately visible state — never a projected success and never a silent half-migrated live system** `[CAN]`. A migration produces its own **replay-verifiable proof** — *an evidentiary record that can be re-derived and checked, NOT a re-executable operation* (`§E15.11`) — and a failed or partial migration resolves to reverse migration, forward repair, parallel run, or an explicitly authorized exception with a named owner.
   - **And partial application can DESTROY the correction path, which is the case this law exists to catch** `[CAN]`. Applying only part of a resource set can mean the application happened, **the history record that reversal depends on was never written**, and the lifecycle hooks that would have proven or gated it were skipped — three consequences in one act. **Two independent mature platforms leave forward repair as the only available resolution after a partial application**, which makes forward repair the *common* case rather than the exotic one.
   - **So `usable_correction_path_exists(...)` is evaluated per execution mode and no single false-reason is canonical** (`§E15.4.3`). **And `landed` may never be read as *proven* or as *reversible*.**
   - **Adapter status is never OMNI's predicate** `[KND]`. A tool reporting `synced`, `applied`, `merged` or `succeeded` supplies an **observation** `[INH §E13.13]`; effect, proof, completeness and reversibility stay derived over OMNI's own owner-scoped facts. *Taken as mechanism, not as its ownership assumptions* (`GRD-033`): no vendor object, mode, wave or proposal semantic is imported, and deployment execution stays Platform's.
5. **Deprecation and withdrawal are separate acts, and their semantics are OWNER-DECLARED** `[CAN]`. **Each subject or claim owner declares its own deprecation and withdrawal semantics — including reversibility, eligibility, notice, effective interval and historical survival.** **No general lifecycle label silently mutates a deployment or erases a prior claim**, and **withdrawal is prospective**: it ends future eligibility and erases neither the released revision, the prior adoptions, the deployments that ran, nor the claims formerly issued `[INH §E14.5]`. *An external standard in which deprecation is reversible and withdrawal is terminal is one owner's declared semantics; it is not a universal OMNI law and is not adopted as one.* **What Output 4 requires is that the owner state exactly what its withdrawal ends.**
6. **★ THE CUMULATIVE-ENVELOPE LAW — the pressure test this output previously left open** `[CAN]`:

   > **For a candidate change admitted under a bounded change or variation envelope, its assessment basis must include the accumulated effect of all prior effective and still-relevant changes governed by that envelope, not only the candidate delta. A change that is individually admissible but would cause the accumulated state to cross an envelope bound is not authorized by the existing envelope, and requires a new or renewed authority basis, a narrowed change, or another governed treatment.**

   **Four consequences** `[KND]`:
   - **the envelope has a pinned baseline and declared bounds** (law above), because *accumulated effect* is meaningless without a fixed origin to accumulate from;
   - **interactions matter, not only sums** — the accumulated basis accounts for how the prior changes interact, and an assessment that evaluates each delta in isolation has not evaluated the envelope;
   - **observed drift or partial application may invalidate the accumulated basis** (`§E15.4.1`'s divergence condition, and law 4 above): where the effective state is not what the envelope's history implies, the accumulated basis is stale and the next admission rests on a fiction;
   - **Output 4 owns this structural requirement and nothing more.** **Aggregation computation, thresholds and conformance testing are Outputs 5 and 6's; no cumulative-risk object, schema or metric is minted here.**

   *An estate that approves a thousand individually-safe changes into one envelope and never re-evaluates the envelope has built the exact failure a pre-authorized change protocol exists to prevent. This is a minimum floor, not an exotic feature: a single device manufacturer operating under a pre-authorized change protocol is already expected to evaluate individual modifications, their interactions and their cumulative impact. Inability to express it would be an OMNI deficiency measured against that floor, not an external requirement expanding OMNI.*

7. **★ PRE-ADOPTION RECONSTRUCTABILITY** `[CAN]`. **Before an irreversible adoption becomes effective, the pre-adoption effective state, the exact assessment basis and the transition basis must remain reconstructable.** *An irreversible act whose prior state cannot be reconstructed has destroyed the only evidence of what was traded away, and the moment that matters is before the act, not after it — which is precisely when nobody wants to stop.* **This may be satisfied by existing immutable history, by prior effective snapshots that still resolve (`§E15.11`), or by any other valid reconstruction path: Output 4 mandates no new snapshot object, no storage mechanism and no checkpoint primitive.** Corroborated by a governance tool in which an irreversible version upgrade cannot proceed until a named milestone of the prior state has been created — **the pre-state is a precondition of the transition, not a courtesy after it.**
8. **★ A CHANGE FREEZE OR ADOPTION LOCKDOWN IS A SEPARATE ENVELOPE, and adoption does not create one** `[CAN]`. **Adoption does not itself suspend the receiving scope's own change authority.** Where a controlled adoption genuinely requires a freeze over overlapping local changes — the real case in which the receiver's configuration cannot move while an upstream revision lands — **that freeze is a separately attributed, authority-bearing, scope-bounded and time-bounded envelope**, carrying an **entry condition** · **affected subjects and scopes** · **authority basis** · **expiry or release condition** · **interruption and failure treatment** · and **preserved prior history.** **A publisher cannot silently impose that freeze on a sovereign receiver** — that would be the `T0-14` violation `§E15.7` law 6 already forbids, arriving through a rollout mechanism instead of through a posture. ***No universal law is stated: most adoptions require no freeze, and asserting one would let every publisher suspend every receiver's autonomy as a side effect of shipping.*** *This is the case where two change lifecycles — the publisher's and the receiver's — cannot both be active over the same subjects, and the resolution is an explicit envelope rather than an implied precedence.*

**Where the deprecation *strategy* lives, stated because this output must not swallow it** `[KND]`: **version-support policy, compatibility windows and deprecation strategy belong to Product / Architecture Governance**, which the Platform capture explicitly declares upstream of and not swallowed by the release plane. **Output 4 supplies the lifecycle contract in which such a policy is expressed and enforced per scope; it does not set the policy, the notice period or the dwell.**

## §E15.9 — External effect, correction and compensation

**Accepted Output 2 reserves this to Output 4 by name: *"Full effect-lifecycle vocabulary is Output 4's; the commitment-versus-effect distinction is Output 2's and cannot be deferred"*** `[INH §E13.2]`.

**The generic grammar. Output 4 owns this shape; domain owners own substantive adequacy** `[KND]`:

> **A compensation, correction, reversal, amendment, remediation or retraction is a NEW act** with its own identity, its own authority basis, its own effective and recorded times, its own effect, and an **explicit typed relation to the original.** **It never overwrites the original effect, and the original effect's outcome is recorded and never revised in place** `[INH §E13.4]`.

**Where the original effect crossed a boundary, its correction crosses the same one** `[INH DEC-036]`. Cross-boundary correction, retraction, supersession, compensation, acknowledgement and remedy concerning an exchange-mediated effect run through **the same governed spine, by reference**: same identity and represented principal, same boundary admission, same capability and delegation, same consent basis, same owning-domain commit, same audit and proof. **The correction is a new attributable act; the external original remains historically resolvable; and substantive commitment and adequacy stay with the source system and the affected domain.** **No capability-contract, context-packet, consent, delegation or proof field is duplicated here, and no second exchange path is created** — *a correction that reached the counterparty by some other route than the effect did is not a governed correction.*

**This shape is inherited from canonical domain law, not invented** `[INH]`: **D6 inv 29 — *"sale immutable post-close; correction = additive adjustment, never edit-in-place"*** (`canonical`), with the rail-agnostic money-state vocabulary already separating `authorized · captured · voided · refund_full · refund_partial · dispute_open · dispute_lost · write_off` as distinct additive facts. **`voided` and `refund_partial` are not the same act and neither restores the pre-sale world.** *Whether Output 4 inherits this as a cited example or generalizes it into cross-cutting law is a question for the Commerce/D6 owner at acceptance, recorded at `§E15.17.2` and not answered here.*

**Four consequences** `[KND]`:

1. **A correction is a new correlated operation** with its own correction identity `[INH §E13.4]`, evaluated under the **currently effective predecessor ruleset** `[INH §E13.15]`. **★ Where the correction requires governed multi-actor work, it is a NEW CORRELATED CHANGE CASE** (`§E15.2.1`) **linked to the predecessor case, the original effects, the admitted evidence and the surviving obligations. It never mutates the predecessor case into a corrected history**, and the predecessor's pinned assessment basis is not rewritten by it. *The estate states the same law from two sides: a closure may be reopened or superseded on new evidence, latent harm, a breached remedy or a failed correction **without erasing the original closure decision and its proof**, and a later adverse outcome does not retroactively brand an earlier reasonable decision negligent.*
2. **Compensation adequacy is not Output 4's to judge.** Whether a credit compensates a settlement, whether a clinical amendment compensates an act performed, and whether a remedy discharges a duty are **Commerce, Care and Accountability decisions.** Output 4 records the posture, the links and the open obligations.
3. **A change in one plane does not propagate to another merely because they are linked** `[INH]`. D6: *payment state ≠ care state* — a payment failure or dispute never by itself ends a care program (`canonical`). **Propagation is determined by the affected owner, never by adjacency.**
4. **Reopening is additive and belongs to the subject's own authority** `[CAN]`. A reopen is a new attributed act under the subject owner's authority; a later correction **links a new state** and does not rewrite the earlier record, decision context, exposure or obligation. *The class-D Care and Accountability captures state both shapes and confer no force.*

### §E15.9.1 — Obligation positions: the cross-cutting non-collapse only

**An obligation is one relational object with several separately held positions. Output 4 states only that they must not be presumed identical, and references Accountability for the model** `[KND]`. Splitting the identity would contradict accepted `§E13.4`'s single obligation identity; collapsing the positions is what lets a party adjudicate its own liability.

**The cross-cutting rule** `[CAN]`: **duty recognition, the obligor position, execution, waiver or discharge, and adequacy are NOT presumed to be held by the same principal, and each must be separately attributable.** In particular:

- **an obligation is recognized and instantiated from a pre-existing basis — law, contract, right, policy, role, prior commitment or attributed decision — and is never manufactured** `[INH G1-FIND-61]`. **A detector emits a candidate, not a duty**; accepted policy may automate the recognition or the instantiation, and never creates the underlying duty;
- **an obligor may author an attributed self-recognition — *we owe this* — and that is a legitimate and valuable act. What an obligor may not be is the exclusive or final authority on whether it owes**, where the duty arises from law, contract, professional obligation, a patient right, a regulator or an adjudicator. *The stronger claim — that an obligor can never own the truth of owing — is rejected as overbroad: it would make voluntary acknowledgment impossible, which is the opposite of the intended safety property;*
- **a contested duty stays representable** `[INH §E12.7.2]`. An obligor's assertion that no duty exists is an **attributed position**, recorded through the orthogonal challenge structure Output 1 already established — never a state change, never automatic discharge, and never automatic establishment either. **Challenge is per-position**: the basis, the recognition, the obligor identity, the party owed, the execution and the adequacy are each independently contestable;
- **adequacy is not the executor's to certify, and not automatically the obligor's or the domain's.** Where the party owed is a patient, an adequacy determination made solely by the operator that owes is self-adjudicated closure. **Output 4 requires that the adequacy authority be named and separately held, and does not name it;**
- **Build OS holds work custody only** `[INH §E13.2]` — *why* an obligation is owed is never *how* the work is carried.

> **The full model is Accountability's, and Output 4 does not duplicate it** `[KND]`. The complete obligation role algebra, waiver and discharge, evidence requirements for discharge, adequacy, transfer, closure and reopen live in the Accountability / governed-reporting-and-resolution lifecycle. **An earlier form of this section reproduced that lifecycle in detail and thereby created a second, competing model of it.** *Reference, do not restate.*

## §E15.10 — When the source, policy, classification or applicability decision changes

**This is `§G1-CONTRACT.c` row 4 — the `G1-FIND-10` vertical thread's Output-4 leg — and it is the obligation, not a side case.**

> **A later source revision, normative-force determination, applicability decision, product classification or operator policy creates a NEW attributable fact. It does not mutate the prior basis, the prior decision, or the effects already produced under it** `[KND]`.

**What Output 4 requires of an external authoritative revision** `[CAN]`:

- **preserve the source's identity and its exact revision** — the revision is part of what was relied on;
- **determine contextual applicability and normative force SEPARATELY from the revision itself.** That a source changed is one fact; that the change applies here, and with what force, are two further facts with their own attribution;
- **preserve prior acts and prior decisions historically** — including recorded refusals, which nothing later erases `[INH G1-FIND-53]`;
- **allow new evidence to invalidate current usability without rewriting prior acceptance** — `accepted_historically` is permanent; `acceptance_currently_usable` is a separate present-tense question `[INH §E13.10]`;
- **keep monitoring, the applicability decision, the recall or corrective decision, and the technical treatment as four distinct acts** (`§E15.5`). ***Monitoring detects. It authorizes nothing.***
- **and appoint no owner.** **Output 4 declares no external-normative layer, no external-normative domain, no owner of law or guidance, and no universal force taxonomy.**
- **★ propagate through the substrate, never by direct scope-to-scope call** `[CAN]`. `CNS_orchestration_contract.md §4` inv 4 and `§5` state it as a binding anti-collapse rule for the coordination layer — *scopes interact ONLY through substrate events, there is no direct scope-to-scope call* — with the event carrying its ownership dimensions and its causal lineage. **Applied to a change: notifying an affected scope is emitting an attributable, ownership-bearing, lineage-carrying event that the receiving scope's own authority then admits or refuses — not reaching into that scope, and not a coordinating surface deciding on its behalf.** This is the **channel** constraint on the selective propagation `§E15.5` already requires: selectivity says *which* scopes are reached, and this says *how*, and together they are what keeps propagation from becoming either a cascade or a back door around local admission `[INH INV-26]`. *CNS reaches the rule from the anti-mega-brain direction and this output reaches it from the sovereignty direction; the constraint is the same one.*

> **★ A BASIS MAY BE CLOSED TO NEW CITATION WHILE ACTS ALREADY CITING IT REMAIN EFFECTIVE — and this is a third thing, not supersession and not invalidation** `[CAN]`. **Three dispositions of an authority basis must stay distinguishable:**
>
> - **superseded** — a newer revision replaces it, and `current_for(scope, as_of)` moves `[INH §E7.1.2`, `§E14.2.1]`;
> - **invalidated** — the basis is determined unsound, and acts resting on it have their **current usability** re-resolved (`§E15.10` step 3) while their history stands;
> - **★ closed to prospective citation** — **no new act may cite the basis, and every act already citing it remains fully effective and is not re-opened.**
>
> **The third is neither of the first two, and no prior clause covered it.** *The mechanism is not hypothetical: a superseded certification-standard version can stop accepting new certifications while every certification already granted against it stays valid indefinitely.* **A basis closure is prospective, attributed, scoped and revision-pinned; it invalidates nothing, corrects nothing and reopens nothing** — and reading it as invalidation would reopen a population of sound prior acts, while reading it as ordinary supersession would let a new act cite a basis that no longer admits new citations. **The closure's own authority, notice and eligibility semantics are the basis owner's** (`§E15.8` law 5's owner-declared form), and **Output 4 states only that the three dispositions must not collapse.**

**Two anti-flattening rules, which are the load-bearing part** `[CAN]`:

1. **The class must not be flattened into one bucket.** Hard clinical or legal regulation, a clinical benchmark or quality measure, a guideline or standard-of-care revision, a payer coverage rule, an accreditation condition and an operator or specialty preference **share a shape — external · versioned · scoped · gates-or-informs — and are not one thing.** *Flattening a clinic preference upward into regulation gives it non-waivable force; flattening a regulation downward into authorized variation launders drift.* **No container object, layer or category is minted here for the class.**
2. **★ Derogability is a facet the SOURCE owns and is never inferred from a label.** *Guidance is guidance; statutes carry exceptions, safe harbours, transition periods, local options and enforcement-discretion positions.* **Where derogability resolves to non-derogable for this actor and circumstance, no exception route may go around it and `§E15.4.4`'s non-derogable floor applies. Where it does not, the exception has a named authority and is an ordinary authorized-exception basis.** *Inferring the floor from the word "regulation" is how a guidance document acquires statutory force.* **The same is true of overridability**: whether a measure, guideline or preference may be overridden, and by whom, is source-owned consequence policy, not a property of its category.

**Seven required steps** `[CAN]`:

1. **Preserve** the prior basis, the prior decisions including refusals, and every effect already produced.
2. **Record** the change as a new attributable source or decision revision, with its own authority basis and both clocks.
3. **Resolve current usability separately from historical validity** `[INH §E13.10]`.
4. **Identify the affected downstream commitments** by impact evaluation over the pinned constituents, producing a completeness **claim** with a declared coverage posture — never a set asserted as complete `[INH §E13.8]`.
5. **Recognize and instantiate owner-scoped obligations — never manufacture them** `[INH G1-FIND-61]`. The available obligations are to revalidate, notify, migrate, supersede, quarantine, stop future use, correct, compensate, or record a lawful exception; each carries the party owed, an obligor, a trigger, a clock, an **authority basis**, and — separately held, per `§E15.9.1` — a waiver authority and an adequacy authority. Each is instantiated only after admission and owner-set resolution, and **a hostile or malformed intake must not place duties on owners** `[INH §E13.3]`. *Stated in the strong form because the alternative is that the change processor becomes the origin of the duties it exists to preserve.*
6. **Preserve unresolved, partial and exception states as separately visible**, including the bidirectional lawful-retention exception where a recipient lawfully refuses or partially executes — completeness honestly includes *reached-but-lawfully-retained-with-exception* and never a false *verified-complete* `[INH C4.4 §R.15]`.
7. **Prohibit projecting the affected area as fully reconciled** until those obligations are accounted for `[INH §E13.10]`.

**Two boundaries** `[KND]`: **origin supersession does not automatically propagate to a receiving scope whose admission pinned the exact prior revision** — that is correct local sovereignty `[INH §E12.7.2]` — and **making that supersession observable to admitters is Output 5's**, per `§E14.9.4`'s routing. Output 4 states the **obligation-recognition law** and builds no observability mechanism. *No surface may call this an obligation-generating law: the change processor recognizes duties, it does not originate them.*

> **What Output 4 would settle for an overlay revision, once its home is ratified — a narrowing rather than a new plane** `[CAN]`. **A policy-overlay revision is not a special case; it is an ordinary subject of this grammar** — a **published revision** by its source authority, **locally admitted** in the receiving scope (`§E15.7`), reaching `effective(scope, …)` through the conjuncts that already exist, **coexisting** under `§E15.8`'s envelope while jurisdictions differ, and **deprecating and withdrawing prospectively** without erasing what was in force. **Output 4 therefore owns the change-lifecycle grammar in which an overlay's own revisions are admitted, coexist, deprecate and withdraw — and owns none of the law.** *Interpretation authority is counsel's, regression-on-legal-change is Build OS's, signal capture is the Evidence Plane's, and substantive thresholds are the domain's and the regulator's.* **The ratified home that owns contextual applicability and force for this class remains OPEN and is recorded at `§E15.17.1`.**

> **★ Bounded self-application, because "architecture operates on itself" must not become infinite regress** `[CAN]`:
>
> - **the currently effective control law governs its own candidate successor**; the successor does not become effective by having been authored;
> - **authority to change the control system is separate from authority exercised BY it**;
> - the successor is evaluated in isolation and simulation where possible, rollout is staged, and break-glass stays attributed and is later reconciled;
> - **the successor becomes effective only on explicit admission and activation.**
>
> *Constitutional amendment, not recursion* — and accepted `§E13.15`'s self-application guard is the source.
>
> **The regulatory form of the same law, stated precisely** `[CAN]`: **the *installed* Architecture Operations system — its executable controls, its decision and change processes, its implementation, and the evidence those processes emit — must itself satisfy the versioning, authority, change-control, validation, risk, monitoring, audit and conformance obligations it imposes on other subjects.** **And the applicable regime is COMPILED, never predeclared**: different regimes govern different parts of the container, and **OMNI may not declare the whole substrate a device, nor assume one regulator governs it.** *This prose dossier is a proposal and is not itself a regulated product; the law is about the installed system.* **Recorded as a distinct requirement and not resolved here.**
>
> **And the authority question is dual** `[KND]`: **who may make the clinical decision** and **who may change the container in which it is made** are different authorities that must never merge — Build OS `09`'s *"build-agent authority never becomes product authority"* is the same law from the build side. **`§G1-AUTH` owns the resolution; `§E15.2` carries the authority-basis reference; Output 4 mints neither.**

## §E15.11 — Reconstruction, replay and fork

**The temporal model is accepted Output 2's and C4.5's. Output 4 reauthors none of it and states only the consequences at change grain** `[INH §E13.5]`. The four temporal questions, the no-hindsight rule that applies to three of them and not to `historical_as_now_reconstructed`, the `resolve(...)` interface with its declared mode and both bounds, the content-addressed snapshot whose mode and bounds sit inside its own input manifest, and the demotion of the snapshot from historical truth to a materialized derivation are all **accepted Output-2 content, referenced here and not restated as new law.** **Full temporal-model reconciliation is `v4_C4_5_temporal_integrity_and_asof_reconstruction_pass_plan.md`'s, whose full pass has not started.**

**Four Output-4 consequences, and only these** `[KND]`:

1. **An assessment or decision basis resolves without hindsight.** Later facts may invalidate `acceptance_currently_usable`, change the observed projection, and cause obligations to be recognized from pre-existing bases. **They may never rewrite what was assessed and approved.** Where an object cannot supply the semantics a declared mode requires, **the request fails rather than returning a confident wrong answer** `[INH §E14.5]`.
2. **No one log, graph, registry, snapshot, projection or dashboard owns historical truth** `[INH §E13.7`, `§E13.5`, `T0-15`, `DEC-033`, `D0THES-GRD-035]`. Historical reconstruction **composes** owner-scoped facts. **The architecture-operation history carries correlation and causal structure. It is not the exclusive owner of what was true.**
3. **A byte revert is not, by itself, a semantic reversal, and it changes no historical interpretation.** It may participate in an authorized reversal when the subject is semantically reversible, the transition is authorized, external effects are accounted for, migration or reverse migration is complete, affected claims and deployments are updated, and **every prior effective snapshot still resolves.** A byte revert that leaves the operation history, the admissions, the adoptions or the claims asserting a state the bytes no longer produce is **drift, unauthorized mutation, partial effect or incomplete treatment** — and under G4 test 10 it is a **FAIL, not a pass.**
4. **★ Reconstruction, replay and fork are three acts that share a starting point and nothing else** `[CAN]`:

| Act | What it is | What it may never do |
|---|---|---|
| **historical reconstruction** | a **read-only derivation** over recorded owner-scoped facts under `resolve(...)` | perform or authorize anything |
| **execution replay** | a **NEW attempt** that happens to start from historical state. It **may** legitimately perform effects **under its own current authority** | **inherit the original act's identity, authority basis, idempotency key or outcome.** It is never a re-read of the first one |
| **forked continuation** | a **new branch** from a prior point. The original history **stays intact** | overwrite, retract or supersede the original by existing; any execution on the branch is **new work** |

> **The precise law, and it is narrower than "replay performs nothing"** `[KND]`: **a replay CAN perform effects. What it cannot do is inherit identity or authority merely because it started from historical state.** Every re-executed non-deterministic or externally consequential step carries **its own attributed authority basis, its own causal lineage to the original, its own effect-scoped idempotency key `[INH §E13.4]`, and its own separately accounted outcome.** *Stating it as "reconstruction performs nothing" would forbid legitimate re-execution and leave the actual hazard — inherited authority — unnamed.*
>
> **Why this is worth stating rather than leaving implied** `[KND]`. A production agent runtime can ship **one verb** that is simultaneously a read, a re-execution of every downstream step including external calls, and a branch. **In an estate whose downstream steps send prescriptions, post charges, notify patients and file submissions, collapsing those three is how a historical query becomes a second clinical act.** *Taken as mechanism, not as its ownership assumptions* (`GRD-033`): **execution attempts and checkpoint mechanics remain Agent Runtime's, external effects remain the emitting boundary's, no checkpoint object is imported, and Output 4 states only that reconstruction confers no execution authority.**
>
> **★ AND THE ESTATE ALREADY USES `replayability` TO MEAN THE FIRST ROW, NOT THE SECOND — a live collision this output would otherwise hand to G2** `[KND]`. The shipped `replayability_preserved` lint in `data_layers_reconciliation_v1.md` requires that **reconciled entities always remain DERIVABLE from the claim ledger, enforced by a mandatory `source_assertion_id` back-pointer on every new reconciled-entity table.** That is **re-derivability — historical reconstruction, row 1** — and it is the substrate's word for it. This section uses **replay** for row 2, *a new attempt that may perform effects.* **Two different acts, one word, and the substrate's usage is the one already in CI.** *A G2 implementer reading both surfaces would satisfy a lint about derivation while believing it had addressed re-execution, which is the single most consequential conflation this section exists to prevent.* **Neither name is corrected here** — the collision is recorded, the substrate's lint is not renamed by this output, and the naming resolution belongs to the temporal reconciliation and the data-substrate owner together.

> **★ THE NO-HINDSIGHT LAW NOW HAS INTERNAL CORROBORATION, AND THE GAP RECORDED ONE PASS AGO IS CLOSED** `[KND]`. The prior pass recorded that `§E15.11`'s no-hindsight rule rested on accepted Output 2 alone and was corroborated by **no internal source yet read** — `data_layers_reconciliation_v1` supplied both time legs and no as-of semantics at all. **`v4_REV184_decision_state_reconciliation.md` supplies it, at spine grade and trifecta-signed-off:** *"outcome-reads-original-context (never rewrites)"* is one of its **seven named spine lines** (`§0.2`), its law states *"outcome later reads the frozen context, never rewrites it"* (`§0.1`), and its round-2 corpus check independently reached **eval the context-packet, not just the answer** — with the operative distinction stated as **reasoning-quality ≠ decision-correctness** (`§R2.3`, `§R3.5`). **So the law is not this output's synthesis and is not Output 2's alone: it is an independently derived, separately signed-off estate line.** *Two consequences worth keeping: the no-hindsight rule is stronger than a query constraint — it is a prohibition on retroactively re-judging a decision by its outcome; and the estate reached it from the accountability direction while `§E13.9` reached it from the temporal direction, which is why neither surface cites the other.* **The as-of RECONSTRUCTION interface is still uncorroborated internally** — `resolve(...)`'s declared mode and both bounds remain accepted Output 2's alone, and nothing read so far states them.

**★ Two further consequences the shipped substrate supplies, recorded because this output stated the weaker form of both** `[KND]`:

5. **The bitemporal asymmetry is the law, and it is sharper than "no universal field set."** Accepted Output 3 prohibits a universal bitemporal field set, which is correct and stops one step short of the reason. The shipped `temporal_truth_pair` lint requires **both** legs on every clinical, observation and decision row while naming them differently: **recorded time is uniformly the row's `created_at`, and effective time is per-subject-kind — `onset_at`, `observed_at`, `decided_at`.** *The asymmetry is not an implementation accident.* **Recorded time is a property of the WRITE, so it is universal, owned by the write boundary, and mechanically enforceable. Effective time is a property of the SUBJECT'S OWN PHYSICS, so it is per-kind and cannot be.** That is exactly why one leg is lintable and the other is a per-object contract — and it means **a change subject may never supply its own recorded time**, which this output had nowhere stated.
6. **Re-derivability is structural, not aspirational, and the mechanism is a back-pointer required at creation time.** `§E15.11`'s consequence 2 says historical reconstruction composes owner-scoped facts. The substrate adds **how that stays true as the estate grows**: a reconciled or derived entity carries a mandatory reference to the authoritative claim it derives from, checked in CI when the table is introduced rather than audited later. **A projection owning no truth `[INH T0-15]` is a prohibition; a required back-pointer to the authoritative basis is the enforceable form of it** — and *the moment to enforce it is table creation, because a derived store without a basis pointer cannot be repaired afterward without re-deriving history that no longer exists.* **No schema, column or lint is imported.**

## §E15.12 — Failure, interruption, partial application and unknown

**Each joined contract declares its own posture for these; they are not one enum, and this section says where each lives** `[KND]`. `C4.4 §R`'s template already requires exactly this declaration per mechanism.

| Outcome | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| `rejected` · `withdrawn` | the deciding authority's decision record — an attributed act, retained as history `[INH §E12.7.2]` |
| `expired` | the grant, condition or envelope that carried the interval. **An expired grant does not erase a decision; it may block a later effect and require reauthorization at the point of consequence** `[INH §E13.10]` |
| `stayed` | a separate authority-bearing stay. **A challenge or dispute alone changes no effective force** `[INH §E12.7.2]` |
| `partially_applied` · `applied_with_exceptions` | the transition's own record, with the exception explicitly named and owned. **Partial or unknown effect is never projected as fully landed** `[INH §E13.10]` |
| `failed` · `abandoned` | the execution record — **Agent Runtime's for runs and attempts, Build OS's for work custody** `[INH §E13.5]`. Architecture Operations references these causally and never re-sources them |
| `disputed` | an **orthogonal attributed challenge resource**, not a lifecycle value `[INH §E12.7.2]`; conflict as a first-class resource `[INH §E14.6]` |
| `unknown` · `unreachable` | **first-class results.** `observed` does not hold for an unreachable target `[INH §E13.10]`; local admission absence is typed absence `[INH §E12.7.2]` |
| `awaiting_evidence` | a durable obligation with a clock and an obligor, **not a lifecycle state of the subject** `[INH §E13.2]` |

**None of these projects as success** `[KND]`. That is the single load-bearing rule of this section, and every row above is an instance of it.

**Survival across interruption can differ by CHANGE KIND, not only by subject** `[CAN]`. Two change kinds applied to the same subject through the same activation mechanism can have different failure physics and different survival behaviour — one persisted for recovery, the other not — which is exactly what `§E15.1`'s splitting rule predicts. **What survives a restart is therefore a property the change kind must declare, not one inferable from the subject alone.**

**Degraded operation is authorized, bounded and separately visible** `[INH §E13.11]`: degraded-mode authority carries bounded, expiring verification debt whose expiry action is conditioned on authority, custody, reversibility and safety; the always-available minimum is stop-what-is-still-controlled, withdraw-unevidenced-claims, preserve-the-debt, escalate. **It may never waive a non-derogable authority, a patient-safety floor, a professional duty, a consent requirement or an independently borne duty.** **`AB-29` — the emergency and degraded-mode regime — is `open`, owned by the Reactor/Care/Agent-Runtime reconciliation owner, and blocks G3.** Output 4 provides the lifecycle slot and does not settle the regime.

> **★ A DECLARED INCIDENT OR EMERGENCY REGIME IS A PARTICIPATING AUTHORITY REGIME — it is not a suspension of the grammar and it originates nothing** `[CAN`, class D]. **Such a regime may accelerate, constrain, stay or compel change activity ONLY through its own pre-established authority basis, scope, expiry, evidence requirements and disclosure obligations.** *It is an ordinary subject of `§E15.7`'s authorized-variation basis and `§E15.3`'s routing, entered under time pressure — not a mode in which those cease to apply.* **Three limits** `[KND]`: **①** it **appoints no cross-cutting commander, and Output 4 mints no incident role** — a coordinating seat is that regime's, and coordination authority is not domain authority: an incident seat that may compel a rollout halt does not thereby acquire the authority to commit clinical, financial or contractual state; **②** it **originates no obligation** — `§E15.9.1`'s recognized-from-a-pre-existing-basis rule holds under emergency exactly as it holds otherwise, and urgency is not a basis; **③** it **may not waive the non-derogable floor** (`§E15.4.4`), and break-glass stays attributed and is later reconciled (`§E15.10`).
>
> **And the evidentiary limb, which is the one that has to be built beforehand or not at all** `[CAN]`: ***what matters in a crisis must already exist as evidence before the crisis*** — the disclosure posture, the authority basis, the affected-set reach and the containment path are **pre-declared or effectively absent**, because a regime that must be constructed while degraded will be constructed by whoever is present. **This is `§E15.7` law 5's pre-declared path and `§E15.8` law 7's pre-adoption reconstructability, stated for the degraded case**, and it is why both are preconditions rather than courtesies. **Output 4 states the relation between the regime and the change; the regime's own content, roles and thresholds are `AB-29`'s, the owning domains' and G3's.**

## §E15.13 — Cessation and survival

**The five non-collapses are inherited and not restated as new law** `[INH §E14.7.4]`: `cessation ≠ deletion` · `succession ≠ sameness` · `replacement ≠ transfer` · `transfer ≠ inheritance of all relations` · `vacancy ≠ implied authority`. **Accepted Output 3 deliberately froze no universal survival enum and routed it here** `[CAN→4]`.

**Survival is a SEMANTIC obligation declared per subject contract, not a field set** `[CAN]`. **Each joined contract states what terminates, what becomes non-current, what survives, what may coexist, what is superseded, what remains legally retained, what becomes unsupported, and which obligations remain open.** **No universal survival enum is proposed, and no mandatory field list is imposed on any subject** — physical record requirements are G2's and the owning domains'.

> **★ CLOSING THE CHANGE WORK DOES NOT CLOSE THE PARTICIPATING LIFECYCLES** `[CAN]`. **Ending, closing or completing the architecture-change work ends, closes and completes nothing else in the case.** The following may survive under their own owners and their own clocks: **supported coexistence · monitoring and recurrence watch · observation debt · support and conformance commitments · migration exceptions · external reliance · patient remedy · compensation · appeal · notification and reporting duties · claim withdrawal · and unresolved or offline receivers.** ***"Change completed" must never be readable as "all consequences complete."***
>
> **★ And the same law one level down, where it is most often broken: EXECUTION TERMINALITY IS NOT OBLIGATION TERMINALITY** `[CAN`, class D]. **`obligation ⟂ fulfillment order ⟂ work order ⟂ task ⟂ run ⟂ attempt ⟂ completion proof`** — seven things, and the estate's canonical Act-loop home separates *the thing owed* from *the thing ordered* as two primitives precisely so this cannot fuse. **Failure, cancellation, timeout, abandonment or successful completion of execution work does NOT by itself close the obligation that work was serving.** *A task can die while what was owed remains owed; a fulfillment order can complete while the obligation it served stays open on its own clock; and a completion proof proves the work happened, never that the duty is discharged.* **An obligation closes only through its rightful owner's applicable terminal disposition — fulfilment, accepted transfer, authorized release or waiver, explicit supersession, or another owner-declared terminal result** — which is `§E15.2.3` clause 2's honest-disposition requirement at execution grain. **And `release state ≠ release authority`**: a domain may record that something was reviewed or released without holding the authority that released it. **No obligation routes to the Act-loop home by default and that home is not a universal custodian** — which obligation lives where is the owning domain's, under `§E15.9.1`'s separately-held positions.
>
> **This is not an Output-4 invention; it is the generalization of a law two domains already hold** `[class D]`. Accountability: **closure ≠ demonstrated prevention** — a case may close for the recipient while recurrence monitoring stays open elsewhere, and a defect may be repaired before the patient's remedy completes; containment, individual remedy, corrective action, durable repair, recurrence monitoring, effectiveness verification and residual-risk acceptance are distinct horizons. Care: **there is no single final closure of the patient's whole relationship — there are scoped completion contracts, one per horizon**, and local completion means every **applicable** condition fulfilled, waived, transferred, superseded or otherwise dispositioned **with no required responsibility silently lost** — explicitly *not* a universal checklist. **Both are `analysis_nonbinding` and confer no force; they defeat this law's novelty and establish that a single universal closure predicate would contradict two domains at once.** **No universal closure predicate or terminal case state is minted here.**

**Two absolute laws** `[KND]`:

1. **No terminal state, by itself, authorizes erasure of provenance, prior effect, prior authority basis, or a recorded refusal.** Revocation is prospective and erases nothing `[INH §E14.5]`. **Payload retention may be altered only by a separate, lawful, authority-bearing retention, redaction, deletion or compelled-forgetting decision** — which must preserve the minimum lawful proof or tombstone where one is required and permitted, and whose substance is **Security + Privacy/Legal's at G3** (`AB-20`, `INV-11`'s redaction limb). **The terminal state is never the authority for erasure; a separate lawful decision is.**
2. **A vacancy blocks; it never defaults upward.** Where a transition's decision condition requires a current eligible holder and none resolves, the transition **fails closed** — `owner_set_complete` does not hold `[INH §E13.8]`, and R8 `§5` states that a role with zero holders makes every dependent gate fail closed. **The authority for a given transition may arise from domain ownership, a local principal's admission authority, cross-cutting acceptance, a bounded integration grant, a claim issuer, a clinical or financial owner, or a non-overridable legal or professional duty** — resolved through the four-function composition per ownership dimension (`T0-13`), **not from a single steward seat.**

## §E15.14 — Decidability of refusal

**The requirement, and it replaces the rejection-ground matrix an earlier form of this output carried as architecture** `[CAN]`:

> **Every consequential transition must expose an attributable, typed, reconstructable reason when it blocks, refuses, stays, invalidates, or requires reauthorization.**

**Three qualifications** `[KND]`. **Attributable** — the refusal names who or what refused, under which basis. **Typed, and the type identity is STABLE** — the reason is a distinguishable kind with a durable identity, not free text, not a boolean, and not a message that can be reworded without notice; a receiver keys behaviour off the reason, so a renamed reason is a breaking change. **Reconstructable** — the refusal can be re-derived later from the facts and revisions that produced it, under `resolve(...)`, without hindsight. **A transition that blocks and cannot say why, on whose authority, or from what state is not governed; it is merely stuck**, and at machine change volume an unexplained refusal is indistinguishable from a defect.

**★ A refusal is not one act by one owner. It decomposes into four positions that are routinely held by different owners, and the estate already ships the decomposition** `[CAN]`. `CNS_orchestration_contract.md §10.1` — `canonical` for orchestration physics — states a live permit-gate in which **the classification flag is Messaging's, the permit-assert is CNS's, the blocker surfacing is D5's `care_state_view`, and the clearing paths are a patient inbound, an audited staff resolution or a deterministic policy.** Four owners, one refusal. Generalized:

| Refusal position | What it holds | Why it does not collapse into the others |
|---|---|---|
| **classification** | the fact that a blocking condition obtains | held by whoever owns the underlying fact, which is usually **not** the refusing surface |
| **assertion** | that this condition blocks *this* transition | the join; the only position that needs to know the intended transition |
| **surfacing** | that the block is visible to whoever is stuck | a projection, owning no truth and conferring no authority `[INH T0-15]` |
| **clearing / discharge** | that the condition no longer obtains | separate from all three, and separately floored — see below |

**Two consequences** `[KND]`. **① The block is an INTERSECTION, not a global flag.** CNS's gate fires only where *what the blocker blocks* intersects *what the permit intends* — a condition can be simultaneously open and irrelevant. This is the same intersection form the runtime supplies at the point of consequence (`§E15.2`), reached independently at refusal grain, and it is what keeps a blocking condition from becoming an estate-wide stop. **② The clearing position carries an actor-class floor.** CNS states it absolutely for one class: *AI output NEVER clears it.* Generalized without importing the domain rule: **for a given consequence class, some actor classes may be structurally ineligible to occupy the clearing position regardless of any grant — and an actor that CAUSED the state is not thereby eligible to clear it.** This is `[INH §E13.11]`'s non-derogable floor located at the discharge position (`§E15.9.1`), and it is narrower than the absolute this output already withdrew: **it is a floor on WHO may discharge for a consequence class, not a prohibition on automating gates.** *CNS is consistent with the withdrawal — its own stage 6 permits AI refinement within constraints, and its stage 4 is an `authority-floor check` rather than an automation ban.*

**★ And the compilation requirement, which replaces the share-of-laws framing** `[CAN]`. **The question is not what percentage of the laws are mechanically decidable.** A share is uninformative when the undecidable remainder may contain every authority, safety, patient-rights and cross-operator decision, and optimizing the share would reward deleting the hard laws. **The requirement is that every retained normative law declare an EXECUTION CLASS — what compilation of it produces — and that a law which declares none is rationale rather than operative law:**

| Execution class | What compiling the law produces |
|---|---|
| **deterministic invariant** | a check over identified inputs that passes or fails |
| **deterministic derivation** | an algorithm over named, owned input facts, with a declared determinism contract `[INH §E13]` |
| **authority adjudication** | a typed decision request naming the rightful owner, inputs, admissible outcomes, evidence, clock and fail-closed behaviour |
| **observation obligation** | required evidence, horizon, attribution, freshness and the disposition route for what is observed |
| **architectural principle** | a binding constraint that must bind through one or more of the above; **standing alone it is rationale** |

**This is not an imported framework — it is the estate's own shipped mechanism generalized.** `CNS §9.2` locks a four-layer separation (rules decide *what* · templates define *what-can-be-said* · AI decides *how within constraints* · humans decide clinical truth) and makes it operational by requiring that **every firing map to exactly one layer, CI-linted**, with a seven-stage execution order in which each stage has defined pass, block and fail behaviour. **A semantic non-collapse participates in operations by forcing every instance to declare its position and be checked — which is precisely what a `X ≠ Y` catalog cannot do and what `§E15.0` already warned about.** Assigning execution classes across the retained laws is **owed before acceptance and NOT performed here**; it is recorded at `§E15.17.1`, and it replaces the share computation that section previously owed.

**The currently discriminating failure conditions** `[CAN]` — these are the conditions that distinguish this proposal from a materially different architecture, and they are the ones a cold implementer must be able to refuse. **They carry no identifiers**: the former `CL-` addresses are retired with the matrix and preserved in git, and no replacement address scheme is minted.

- a **stored lifecycle scalar** from which acceptance, landing, effectiveness, conformance, reconciliation or authority is inferred (`§E15.2`, `§E15.3`);
- **absence read as permission**, or **absence used to establish architecture-change identity** (`§E15.3`);
- a **classification result with no attributed determining authority or basis**, or an unresolved classification treated as a default rather than as a block (`§E15.3`);
- an **assessment treated as the approval artifact**, or an assessment issuer treated as a deciding authority (`§E15.4.1`);
- a **decision whose assessment basis lacks stable identity or cannot be exactly reconstructed**, or a basis that copies substantive state rather than referencing it (`§E15.4.1`);
- a **simulated result recorded, projected or relied on as observed consequence** (`§E15.4.1`);
- a **silent user-impacting release represented as a shadow execution, or as no-effect** (`§E15.4.1`);
- **exposure proceeding while a required exposure classification or exposure authority is unresolved** (`§E15.4.1`, `§E15.3`);
- **authority to expose read as authority to commit** the resulting clinical, financial, legal, contractual or operational state (`§E15.4.1`);
- an **observation-gated escalation whose observation horizon exceeds the escalation interval**, presented as evidence-gated (`§E15.4.1`);

- a **resolved desired fleet state treated as activation**, or a global approval used as per-target eligibility (`§E15.7`);

## §E15.15 — Machine volume: idempotency, concurrency and duplicate transitions

**At machine change volume the lifecycle must compose with accepted Output 2's identity and idempotency law rather than build a second engine** `[INH §E13.4]`.

> **★ THE SCALE INVARIANT, and it is one sentence** `[CAN]`:
>
> > **Semantic correctness must not depend on global enumeration, global consensus, a global lock, or a single authoritative clock.**
>
> **★ The scale variable is AUTHORITY-BOUNDARY DENSITY AND TRUST-DOMAIN DISCONTINUITY — and the estate already named it, better than a generic volume list** `[CAN`, class D]. The load-bearing measures are **the number of independently owned domain records · the number of distinct trust anchors · the number of jurisdictional and policy profiles · the degree of incentive conflict · the cross-organization portability requirement · reversibility and blast radius · the number of custody transfers · the number of execution rails · and the probability that a failure changes the domain world-model.** Volume, owner fan-out, evidence latency, human-review scarcity and duration matter, and they are not the discriminator.
>
> ***The grammar's value rises with trust-domain discontinuity and unresolved-custody risk — not with the number of corporate logos, and not with revenue.*** `[KND]` **A single organization contains many trust domains** — professional licensure, dispensing authority, payer adjudication, banking settlement, jurisdictional regulation, affected-party authorization, facility policy — **and several organizations may share one trust framework.** *An estate that optimizes for "many companies" has optimized for the wrong axis: the hard case is the boundary count, and boundaries exist inside one operator. Revenue is not an architecture variable at all — a large estate and a small one differ on the measures above, and the grammar has to hold on all of them or it holds on none.*
>
> **The structural invariants that follow — these are Output 4's** `[CAN]`:
>
> - **no global serialization point is required to establish change identity** — correlation identity is assigned by its owner, not by a queue everything passes through;
> - **no fleet-complete enumeration is required before a legitimate local fact may be recorded** — a sovereign receiver's admission is valid whether or not the publisher has finished counting receivers;
> - **no fleet-global lock or consensus is implied by one correlated case** — a case is a correlation, not a distributed transaction, and accepted Output 2 already carries **no atomicity claim whatsoever**;
> - **no single authoritative timeline is implied** — effective time resolves per scope under the declared mode, and there is no false total order `[INH §E13.5`; C4.5];
> - **partial computation carries partial coverage and may never project semantic completeness** (`§E15.4.4`);
> - **unreachable, overloaded, delayed or uncomputed regions produce attributed `unknown`, a blocking posture, or durable debt — never optimistic success** (`§E15.12`);
> - **aggregate results are qualified by scope, temporal mode, aggregation policy and coverage** (`§E15.2.1` law 5);
> - **later local or finer-grained facts remain admissible after an aggregate is published, and may invalidate it without rewriting it** (`§E15.11`);
> - **and any reduction of coverage caused by cost, capacity or burden is explicit, policy- or authority-bearing, and visible in the result** — *a projection that got cheaper by looking at less must say so, because a silent coverage reduction is indistinguishable from a healthy estate.*
>
> **What is NOT Output 4's, and is routed rather than implied** `[KND]`: graph partitioning · incremental and differential computation · caching · indexing · materialization strategy · scheduling · cost budgets · thresholds · and every algorithm → **Outputs 5 and 6 and G2.** **Output 4 requires no universal enumeration, and equally forbids none: enumerating a genuinely bounded case is legitimate, and the invariant is only that correctness never depends on it.**

> **★ HOW THE NO-GLOBAL-ATOMICITY LAW IS ACTUALLY REALIZED, because the estate settled it and this output carried only the prohibition** `[KND]`. Accepted Output 2 forbids one globally atomic transaction, which is right and leaves open how a commitment and its cross-boundary effects stay consistent without one. **`data_layers_reconciliation_v1.md` records the decision as LOCKED and shipped: the owner's canonical write is atomic in ONE local transaction, the outbound effect is enqueued as a row IN THAT SAME TRANSACTION, and workers retry it under effect-scoped idempotency.** **Local atomicity plus a transactional outbox is the mechanism that makes owner-scoped commitment work without global atomicity** — the commitment and the *intent* to produce its external effect commit together, and the effect itself completes asynchronously, retryably, and never silently. Two consequences for this output: **①** *a commitment with no durably enqueued effect intent is not a partial success — it is a lost effect*, which is the shape `§E15.12` calls partial application and the substrate refuses structurally; and **②** the retry boundary is exactly where `§E15.15`'s unknown-effect law lives, so **the outbox row is the object that makes "did the external effect happen" answerable at all.** *No outbox table, worker, queue or job vocabulary is imported* — the mechanism is recorded and the shipped names stay with the data substrate.

> **★ FEEDBACK-BEARING CHANGE ACTIVITY NEEDS A DECLARED ENVELOPE, AND A SHORT PASS PROVES NOTHING ABOUT A LONG ONE** `[CAN`, class D]. **Where change activity is repeated, feedback-bearing or self-modifying — a change whose output conditions the next change, an automated remediation that re-enters its own intake, a correction loop that re-triggers assessment — it carries a declared operating envelope, a stop or containment condition, an observation horizon, and the evidence permitting continued operation.** **Two limbs, and the second is the one estates get wrong:**
>
> - ***Amplification is the failure mode, not error.*** A loop that is individually correct at each iteration can still diverge if the quantity it feeds back on grows — the cumulative-envelope law (`§E15.8`) stated over iteration rather than over admissions, and the reason `§E15.5`'s *monitoring detects, it authorizes nothing* has to hold even when the monitor is fast enough to act.
> - ***A low-volume or short-duration pass is not evidence of production or long-horizon stability.*** **The conditions that trigger a rare failure are, by construction, rare** — a defect that manifests in one run in a hundred thousand is invisible to every pass short enough to be convenient, and its absence from a pilot is not evidence of its absence at fleet volume. *This composes with the observation-horizon clause (`§E15.4.1`): there the horizon is longer than the escalation interval; here the trigger is rarer than the sample.*
>
> **Output 4 sets no numeric criterion, no gain bound, no iteration cap and no sampling rule** — the source's own stability criterion is specific to a model-architecture recurrence and is **expressly not adopted as OMNI law.** **What transfers is the requirement that a feedback-bearing change path declare its envelope and its stop condition rather than inherit them.** Enforcement, numeric bounds and detection are **Agent Runtime's, Platform E&V's, Output 6's and G4's**.

- **Submission is idempotent; judgment is not.** A retried submission after a timeout produces **one** decision — otherwise a network failure manufactures consent. A genuinely changed position produces a **new decision revision that supersedes**, with both surviving in history. `G1-FIND-47`, tagged `[CAN→4 · lifecycle]`, is proposed as resolved here **in the lifecycle grammar** and remains open while this output is `PROPOSED · NOT_ACCEPTED`.
- **Effect idempotency is effect-scoped, never change-scoped** `[INH §E13.4]`. The operation identity is not an idempotency key for anything.
- **Deterministic derivations are identified by a result digest over pinned inputs under a declared determinism contract; digest equality *is* the idempotency** `[INH §E13.4]`. Claiming digest equality for a nondeterministic function is the same defect as hand-authoring a derived value.
- **★ Distinct fact ownership permits concurrency; it does not prove non-conflict** `[INH §E13.11]`. Same-fact/same-scope overlap is a **guaranteed** collision class and one must fail. But accepted Output 2 states plainly that *"base movement and file disjointness are not collision control: two proposals can be file-disjoint and semantically contradictory, based on different owner or policy revisions, modifying different descriptions of the same logical resource, individually conforming and jointly invalid, or competing to supersede the same relation."* **Concurrency is therefore admissible only after semantic-collision, constraint, ordering and atomicity-group evaluation over the inherited envelope** — protected logical resource set · overlapping-operation detection · atomicity groups · ordering dependencies · a semantic conflict object · a rightful resolver · re-evaluation conditions. **Version-control tooling, merge queues and branch mechanics are adapters underneath that envelope, never the model.**
- **Stale-base rejection** `[CAN]`: a transition evaluated against a base whose pinned constituents no longer match what it required is rejected by the **invalidation predicate**, which requires no write anywhere `[INH §E13.9`, `§E14.5]`.
- **Retry without double effect** `[CAN]`: retry is permitted where the effect key is stable and the boundary is idempotent, **or where there is resolved evidence that the prior attempt did not produce the effect, or a rightful reconciliation or compensation authorization covers it**; where none holds, the transition resolves to `unknown` and a durable obligation, never an optimistic success. **★ And the negative half, which the identity law above makes necessary** `[CAN]`: ***a new run or operation identity does not sanitize a duplicate consequence.*** **An unchanged decision basis is necessary for a retry to stay inside its run; it is NOT sufficient for the retry to be SAFE** — those are two different questions and only the first is about identity. **After an attempt capable of crossing a commitment frontier, silence is not exoneration: a timeout, a missing acknowledgement, a transport error or an unknown outcome is evidence of nothing about the world**, and `§E15.7`'s chain already says delivery implies no acknowledgement while `§E15.12` already says `unknown` never projects as success. *The composition matters more than either half: the identity law mints a fresh run when the basis changes materially, and without this clause a reader could take the fresh identity as a fresh effect ledger — which is exactly how a duplicate charge, a duplicate order, a duplicate patient contact and a duplicate external commitment get manufactured at fleet volume by a system behaving correctly at every individual step.* **Effect idempotency stays effect-scoped and is untouched by any run, attempt or operation identity.**
- **Causation is explicit, never inferred from time order** `[INH §E13.5]` — receipt presence cannot establish causal order.

> **★ THE EXECUTION IDENTITIES DO NOT COLLAPSE INTO THE CHANGE, AND A RETRY IS NOT A LOOPHOLE** `[CAN`, class D]. **`architecture change ⟂ resolution or decision ⟂ agent run ⟂ execution attempt ⟂ tool call ⟂ emitted external effect`** — six identities with different owners, and `§E15.12` already routes runs and attempts to Agent Runtime and work custody to Build OS. **What Output 4 adds is the boundary at which a retry stops being one:** *a retry may remain within one run only while the decision, scope, authority, constraints, decision basis and intended effect are **materially unchanged**.* **A material change in any of them creates a NEW linked run or correlated operation under the rightful owner — never an invisible retry**, because the alternative is a changed decision executing under an authorization granted for a different one. *This is `§E15.15`'s submission-idempotent/judgment-not law at execution grain, and `§E15.11`'s replay-inherits-no-authority law seen from the other side.*

> **★ A CHECKPOINT, COMPACTION, HANDOFF OR RESTART CREATES NOTHING AND INHERITS NOTHING AUTOMATICALLY** `[CAN`, class D]. **Continuing across one of those events does not by itself create a new architecture change, resolution or operation** — *continuity is not a change.* **But continuation may inherit the prior operation's authorization only while identity and principal · subject and scope · unresolved obligations · current authority and decision basis · causal and evidence references · known external-effect posture · exact changed artifacts · and the authorized effect envelope remain RECONSTRUCTABLE and, where applicable, materially unchanged.** **Where any of those is lost or has materially changed, the prior authorization does not silently survive the gap** — a new linked run, a reassembled basis or a re-resolution is required, and the loss itself is recorded rather than inferred away. ***And the sharpest limb: a regenerated summary may support navigation and may never replace, rewrite or manufacture the evidence continuation depends on.*** *This is the estate's own recurring leak-at-pivots failure stated at change grain — a compaction that silently substitutes an ungrounded summary for evidence is not a continuation, it is an unattributed re-authoring, and at machine volume the pivot is where authorization is most likely to be inherited by something that can no longer show why it holds.* **The checkpoint's contents, retention and mechanics are Agent Runtime's and Build OS's; Output 4 states only that inheritance is conditional and that its conditions are evidentiary.**

> **★ MID-EXECUTION INVALIDATION IS PROSPECTIVE AND REWRITES NOTHING** `[CAN`, class D]. **Changed authority, revoked policy, altered subject state, withdrawn evidence or expired trusted context may invalidate CONTINUED USE and FUTURE ADMISSIBILITY, may invalidate caches, materializations and derived projections, and may pause, terminate, narrow or require a freshly assembled basis — and may never erase or rewrite the events and effects that already occurred.** *The record of what an execution actually saw and did is immutable historical evidence; what is withdrawn is permission to keep going and permission to rely on it later.* **The transition itself is recorded**, and — the runtime's own sharpest limb — **revocation propagates at least as aggressively as publication did.** **The invalidating owner reconsiders its own accepted state; the executing layer is a propagation target and a proposer, never the reconsideration authority** (`§E15.5`'s *monitoring detects, it authorizes nothing*, at execution grain). **No taint engine, no central invalidation service and no cascade is implied** (`§E15.5`'s selective propagation governs).

> **★ MACHINE-PRODUCED MATERIAL CARRIES ITS PRODUCING CONTEXT'S FORCE UNTIL A RIGHTFUL AUTHORITY ADOPTS IT** `[CAN`, class D]. **A machine-generated assessment, recommendation, patch, migration, correction proposal or proof retains the force of the context that produced it — it does not acquire force by being good.** **Delegation may NARROW authority and may never WIDEN it**, a delegated child never inherits more than its parent, the parent stays accountable, and **the default ceiling is propose-only against owned truth.** ***Evidence quality never self-promotes a candidate into an authoritative transition***, and improved confidence is not a promotion event. *This is the machine-volume form of `§E15.4.1`'s candidate → admission chain and the reason `§E15.2.3` clause 5b's automation law bites on origination rather than on execution: **at fleet scale the volume of well-made proposals is exactly what makes an unattributed promotion path catastrophic.*** **Adoption is the owning authority's act; Output 4 states only that the ceiling exists and that crossing it is an attributable act.**

## §E15.17 — Current state, unresolved seams, boundary, proof, source posture and STOP

**Current state.** **Output 4 is `PROPOSED · NOT_ACCEPTED`.** **G1 is OPEN and INCOMPLETE.** **`§G1-AUTH` is MANDATORY and INCOMPLETE — partially converged.** **Output 5 is NOT STARTED.** No carry is discharged, no ledger row is closed, every enumerated value set remains `[CAN]`, and **nothing is installed** — no schema, registry, index, stable-address scheme, validator, workflow, generator, route, gate, checkpoint, lane, registry row, contract, code or artifact is created by this proposal.

**What the proposal now carries, stated as current shape rather than as a history of passes** `[KND]`. **One bounded purpose** with explicit rejections (`§E15.0`) · a **distinguishability contract** rather than a register, with one owner per fact and **holder coincidence collapsing nothing** (`§E15.1`) · a **reference algebra that imposes no state model** (`§E15.2`) · an **admission seam** stating the minimum semantic result and owning no classifier (`§E15.3`) · **prospective ⟂ simulated ⟂ observed** discriminated by the frontier, with **visibility, exposure, consequence and authority as four orthogonal axes** and the **observation horizon** as an input to escalation (`§E15.4.1`) · record-grain ownership and the three separations (`§E15.4.2`) · the legacy profiles and derived correction paths (`§E15.4.3`) · **coverage honesty including the recorded null** (`§E15.4.4`) · cross-scope reuse through two pathways and no third path through silence (`§E15.4.5`) · the **treatment non-collapse laws**, now including **disclosure ⟂ technical correction** and **monitoring's governed intake** (`§E15.5`) · the **commitment frontier** as discrete events (`§E15.6`) · the **publication → disclosure → delivery → acknowledgement → admission → adoption → deployment → activation → effective use → support → conformance** partial order with the **change-intelligibility laws** (`§E15.7`) · **coexistence, migration, the cumulative envelope, pre-adoption reconstructability and the separately authorized freeze** (`§E15.8`) · correction as a new linked act and the obligation non-collapse referenced to Accountability (`§E15.9`) · external-authoritative change with **no owner, layer or taxonomy appointed** (`§E15.10`) · **reconstruction ⟂ replay ⟂ fork** (`§E15.11`) · failure, survival and decidability (`§E15.12`–`§E15.14`) · and machine-volume composition (`§E15.15`).

**Both compatibility axes, the cumulative-envelope law, the intelligibility chain, the visibility axis and the observation horizon are the laws this output most recently lacked.** **No index, registry, law table, stable-address scheme, schema, validator, generator or CI job is any part of it.** **Rationale and evidence live in this section and in git; no essential qualification of any law above exists outside this carrier.**
